vici:vici-10380.description: Long identified as Nida's forum, this central complex is now known from recent excavations to have been a multi-phase religious precinct of at least eleven temple buildings with ritual pits, not a conventional marketplace.

vici:vici-10449.label: Forum Ladenburg [Lopodurum]
vici:vici-10449.description: The forum and basilica of Lopodunum, capital of the Civitas Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium, formed by c. AD 220 the largest known Roman building complex in southern Germany, roughly 130 x 84 m.

vici:vici-10516.label: Plovdiv Forum Romanum [Philipopolis]
vici:vici-10516.description: Built under Vespasian in the 1st century AD, the 20-hectare forum of Philippopolis is the largest Roman forum in Bulgaria; 1971 excavations uncovered an odeon, a library, and an altar to Demeter and Kore.
vici:vici-10516.wikidataDescription: historic Roman plaza in the city of Plovdiv, Bulgaria

vici:vici-10605.label: Forum (Arles)
vici:vici-10605.description: Forum of Roman Arelate, laid out around 30-20 BC at the crossing of the cardo and decumanus. A 1951 find of a marble copy of Augustus's clipeus virtutis (26 BC) confirms its imperial-cult role; its cryptoporticus survives beneath Place du Forum.

vici:vici-10763.label: Markt  Lugdunum Convenarum
vici:vici-10763.description: The macellum (market hall) of Lugdunum Convenarum, built beside the forum, burned and was rebuilt in the 2nd century, then destroyed in the 4th; at 55 by 26 m it is the largest known Roman market building in the western provinces.

vici:vici-10764.label: Erstes Forum Lugdunum Convenarum
vici:vici-10764.description: The older, simpler of Lugdunum Convenarum's two forums, laid out in the early Augustan period on the hilltop oppidum tied to Pompey's original garrison; a trophy marking Augustus's Pyrenean victories may have stood at this symbolically charged site.

vici:vici-10765.label: Zweites Forum Lugdunum Convenarum
vici:vici-10765.description: The larger, later forum of Lugdunum Convenarum, built in the lower town as the colony expanded under Augustus and Tiberius, centred on a temple oriented toward the earlier forum.

vici:vici-10800.label: Forum Carteia
vici:vici-10800.description: Forum of Carteia, first Latin colony founded outside Italy (171 BC) at the head of the Bay of Gibraltar; imperial-era remains include tabernae flanking one of Andalusia's largest fora, near baths and a hillside theatre.

vici:vici-11040.label: Forum of Theodosius
vici:vici-11040.description: Built by Constantine I as the Forum Tauri and rebuilt by Theodosius I after 393 on the model of Trajan's Forum in Rome; its 40-50 m triumphal column stood until the late 15th century, with fragments surviving near Beyazit Square, Istanbul.
vici:vici-11040.wikidataDescription: Roman forum and triumphal column in Constantinople (Istanbul, Turkey)

vici:vici-11217.label: Forum Tarracone
vici:vici-11217.description: Colonial forum of Tarraco, civic centre of the Roman colony in the lower town; an early Republican square dedicated to the Capitoline Triad was replaced under Tiberius by a larger square fronted by a three-aisled basilica.

vici:vici-11220.label: Forum Kolonialen Tarraco
vici:vici-11220.description: The forum of the Roman colony at Tarraco, distinct from the provincial forum above it, held a basilica, curia and a Capitoline temple to Jupiter, Juno and Minerva; destroyed by fire in late antiquity and never rebuilt.

vici:vici-11236.label: Forum Cartegena
vici:vici-11236.description: Forum of Carthago Nova, excavated on the Molinete hill since 1982, held a temple to the Capitoline Triad, a curia, and the Augusteum, a college devoted to the cult of Augustus; a site museum opened in 2021.

vici:vici-11277.label: Forum Torreparedones
vici:vici-11277.description: Forum of the Roman colony identified with Colonia Virtus Iulia Ituci, paved in the 1st century AD under Tiberius; an inscription credits Marco Junio Marcelo with financing the pavement, and its north portico yielded a Julio-Claudian dynastic statue group.

vici:vici-11584.label: Forum Maktar
vici:vici-11584.description: Mactaris' second, porticoed forum (about 1,500 sq m) is entered through the Arch of Trajan, dedicated in AD 116 to mark the city's changed status; the arch was later incorporated into Byzantine-era fortifications.

vici:vici-11615.label: Cryptoporticus und Forum Romanum - Arles
vici:vici-11615.description: Three U-shaped vaulted galleries built around 30-10 BC to level uneven ground beneath the forum of Roman Arelate (Arles); used for storage and structural support, they are among the best-preserved Roman substructures, part of the city's UNESCO listing.

vici:vici-11811.label: Forum - Tipasa
vici:vici-11811.description: Forum of Roman Tipasa (76m by 43m) with porticoes on three sides and a capitolium on the fourth, alongside a curia and civil basilica; part of the coastal city, UNESCO World Heritage-listed since 1982.

vici:vici-11826.label: Forum Colonia Julia Aurelia Commoda
vici:vici-11826.description: Forum, about 55m square with a Corinthian portico, of Thuburbo Majus, which was elevated to colony status as Colonia Julia Aurelia Commoda under Commodus in AD 188; its Capitolium to Jupiter, Juno and Minerva was dedicated in AD 168.

vici:vici-11882.label: Forum - Cherre'
vici:vici-11882.description: Market-forum of the rural Gallo-Roman sanctuary complex at Cherré near Aubigné-Racan, which also had a theatre, temples and baths, built from the late 1st century AD and excavated since 1977; apparently without permanent habitation.

vici:vici-13911.label: Forum Aquileia
vici:vici-13911.description: Forum of Roman Aquileia (colony founded 181 BC), monumentalized in the 1st century AD with porticoes carved with Medusa and Jupiter Ammon reliefs; its location was lost after antiquity and rediscovered only in the 1930s.

vici:vici-14029.label: Forum of Sarmizegetusa
vici:vici-14029.description: Forum of Ulpia Traiana Sarmizegetusa, capital of Roman Dacia founded c. 108-110 AD under Trajan; a monumental gated courtyard with emperor statues led to a basilica (tribunal) and curia where the city council met.

vici:vici-14877.label: Cryptoporticus Forum Augusta Prætoria Salassorum
vici:vici-14877.description: Horseshoe-shaped underground gallery (c. 90x73m) with twin barrel-vaulted aisles on travertine pillars, encircling the sacred forum precinct of Augusta Praetoria (founded 25 BC); rediscovered in the early 1900s by archaeologist Ernesto Schiaparelli.

vici:vici-17023.label: Jublains, forum
vici:vici-17023.description: Forum of Noviodunum, Augustan-era capital of the Diablintes, built alongside a theatre and baths as the town was urbanized in the later 1st century AD; the site's 3rd-century castellum fort remains its most prominent standing structure.

vici:vici-17067.label: Gisacum, forum
vici:vici-17067.description: Forum of the Gallo-Roman sanctuary town of Gisacum, built during the site's major early-2nd-century rebuilding; comprised several colonnaded squares serving a monumental sanctuary complex rather than a self-governing civic capital.

vici:vici-17379.label: Aglasun,Bouleterion,TR - SAGALASSOS
vici:vici-17379.description: Bouleuterion (council house) of Sagalassos, built c. early 1st century BC and seating roughly 220 councillors on tiered benches along three sides; superseded as the council's meeting place by the Odeon after c. 200 AD.

vici:vici-17493.label: Foro di Veleia
vici:vici-17493.description: Forum of Veleia, paved under Augustus by magistrate Lucius Licinius Priscus with a portico of heated shops; excavations from 1760, prompted by the Tabula Alimentaria bronze find, uncovered it complete with basilica and Julio-Claudian statues.

vici:vici-17498.label: Foro Camunnorum
vici:vici-17498.description: Forum of Civitas Camunnorum (Cividate Camuno), built in the late 1st century AD and used until c. 350 AD; its c. 80m-long 'forum palace' facade held statue niches for the imperial family, excavated in 2008.

vici:vici-18052.label: Agora, Ptolemais
vici:vici-18052.description: The agora of Ptolemais, one of the five cities of Cyrenaica's Pentapolis; nearby stood the Palazzo delle Colonne, a lavish governor's residence spanning the Hellenistic to Byzantine periods.

vici:vici-18189.label: South Agora, Miletus
vici:vici-18189.description: The largest agora in the Greek world, 164 x 196 m and ringed by stoas; its 2nd-century AD monumental gate, built under Hadrian, was excavated by German archaeologists and now stands reconstructed in Berlin's Pergamon Museum.

vici:vici-18736.label: Forum
vici:vici-18736.description: A late-1st-century Roman market building outside the eastern gate of the Nijmegen legionary fortress: a colonnaded rectangular square with twin monumental columns, abandoned around 100 AD as trade shifted to the new settlement of Noviomagus.

vici:vici-19177.label: Forum CCAA
vici:vici-19177.description: The forum of Roman Cologne (Colonia Claudia Ara Agrippinensium), spanning roughly six insulae at the crossing of the cardo and decumanus, closed on its west side by a massive ring-shaped cryptoporticus about 135 m across.

vici:vici-19275.label: Foro romano (Vicenza)
vici:vici-19275.description: The forum of Roman Vicetia, paved in trachyte slabs from the Euganean Hills; a fragment was uncovered in 1987 beneath Palazzo Trissino-Baston and excavated by Veneto's archaeological superintendency in 1989.

vici:vici-19485.label: Forum Londinium
vici:vici-19485.description: London's Roman forum-basilica, rebuilt around 90-120 AD into a 168 x 167 m square with a three-storey basilica — reputedly the largest north of the Alps until Trier's forum surpassed it.

vici:vici-21190.label: Roman forum with porches
vici:vici-21190.description: Part of the Aquae Iasae spa complex around a thermal spring, this forum with porticoes stood beside a capitolium with temples to Jupiter, Juno and Minerva; excavated since 1953, it flourished 1st-4th century AD before Gothic raiders damaged it.

vici:vici-22179.label: Roman forum at Fulfinum
vici:vici-22179.description: The forum of Municipium Flavium Fulfinum, a Flavian veteran colony on Krk; its main temple, dedicated to the Capitoline Triad, anchored a 1,300 m² square that stayed in civic use into the 5th century AD, when a Christian basilica rose nearby.

vici:vici-22237.label: Agora of Metropolis near Yeniköy (Turkey)
vici:vici-22237.description: Roman-era agora of Metropolis in Ionia, excavated since 1989; Doric colonnaded porticoes and 2nd-century CE mosaic pavements mark it as the city's commercial hub, used until earthquake destruction in the 5th–6th century.

vici:vici-22458.label: Agora of Amathous [Amathus]
vici:vici-22458.description: Marketplace of the Cypriot city-kingdom of Amathus, excavated 1977–1991 and 2001–2003 by Cypriot and French teams; a Doric west portico of thirteen columns led to a nymphaeum, its water supply repaired under Hadrian.

vici:vici-23654.label: Trier, Forum
vici:vici-23654.description: Civic square of Augusta Treverorum (Trier), 275 x 135 m across three city blocks, expanded in the late 1st and mid-2nd centuries; a 100 x 25 m basilica was added around 300 CE under Constantius Chlorus or Constantine I.

vici:vici-23968.label: Episcopal Adminstration at Apamea
vici:vici-23968.description: Bishop's residence adjoining the Eastern Cathedral complex at Apamea, which grew in importance after the city became capital of Syria Secunda and seat of an archbishopric in the early 5th century AD.

vici:vici-24002.label: Dur Sharrukin Palace
vici:vici-24002.description: Palace of the Assyrian king Sargon II, centerpiece of his new capital Dur-Sharrukin, built c. 717-706 BC on a raised platform covering some 9 hectares with about 200 rooms; discovered in 1843 by Paul-Émile Botta.

vici:vici-24012.label: Nimrud, Southwest Palace
vici:vici-24012.description: Unfinished royal residence built by the Assyrian king Esarhaddon (r. 680-669 BC) in the southwest corner of the citadel of Kalhu (Nimrud), reusing carved stone reliefs stripped from the earlier Northwest Palace of Ashurnasirpal II.

vici:vici-24015.label: Niniveh - Ninuva
vici:vici-24015.description: Sennacherib's "Palace Without Rival" at Nineveh, built from 703 BC, roughly 450 x 220 m with at least 80 sculpture-lined rooms; excavated by Austen Henry Layard in 1845-1851 and later housed the archives/library used by Ashurbanipal.

vici:vici-24048.label: Emona forum
vici:vici-24048.description: Central square of the Roman colony of Emona (founded c. 14 CE) in modern Ljubljana, laid out at the crossing of its cardo and decumanus maximus; its remains now lie beneath the Ferant Park apartment blocks.

vici:vici-24082.label: Constantinople, Augusteôn Square
vici:vici-24082.description: Constantinople's ceremonial square between Hagia Sophia and the imperial palace, carved by Constantine from Septimius Severus's Tetrastoon; rebuilt by Leo I in 459 and by Justinian I in the 530s after Nika-riot destruction, with Justinian's honorific column erected in 543.

vici:vici-24100.label: Agora of Notion
vici:vici-24100.description: Marketplace of the Ionian city of Notion, under excavation by the University of Michigan since 2022; work has focused on a courtyard house on its west side and the bouleuterion on its east side.

vici:vici-24171.label: Western Agora of Miletus
vici:vici-24171.description: One of Miletus's two agoras, dating to the end of the Hellenistic period near the city's stadium and Temple of Athena, with further monumental building added under the Roman Empire.

vici:vici-24173.label: South Agora of Miletus
vici:vici-24173.description: The largest agora in the Greek world (164 x 196 m), built under Antiochus I in the 3rd century BCE; it held the bouleuterion, temples, and a nymphaeum, entered through the monumental Miletus Market Gate.

vici:vici-24215.label: Agora of Assos
vici:vici-24215.description: Assos's 2nd-century BC agora was cut into a terrace with Doric stoas on its north and south sides and a bouleuterion at the east end; the theatre lay just south, overlooking the Aegean.

vici:vici-24225.label: State Agora, Ephesus
vici:vici-24225.description: Ephesus's civic State Agora, first laid out in the 6th century BC and rebuilt in Roman style by the 1st century BC; its surviving north-side Basilica Stoa was dedicated in 11 CE by C. Sextilius Pollio.

vici:vici-24341.label: Agora of Termessos
vici:vici-24341.description: Central paved agora of Termessos, flanked by the Hellenistic stoas of Attalos II and of a citizen named Osbaras, near the city theatre; Termessos famously repelled a siege by Alexander the Great in 333 BC.

vici:vici-24410.label: Agora of Side
vici:vici-24410.description: Side's agora is centred on a round 2nd-century BC temple to Tyche and Fortuna with twelve columns; in the late Hellenistic period the square also served as a slave market for Cilician pirates.

vici:vici-24423.label: Agora of Side
vici:vici-24423.description: Side's agora is centred on a round 2nd-century BC temple to Tyche and Fortuna with twelve columns; in the late Hellenistic period the square also served as a slave market for Cilician pirates.

vici:vici-24442.label: Agora of Alabanda
vici:vici-24442.description: The agora of Alabanda (c. 112 x 72 m), unearthed in 1904 by Halil Edhem Bey, lies just south of the city's rectangular bouleuterion in this Carian city founded in the 4th century BC.

vici:vici-24456.label: Lower Agora, Sagalassos
vici:vici-24456.description: One of Sagalassos's two public squares, excavated from 1990 under Marc Waelkens's Leuven-led project alongside the Upper Agora; the Lower Agora adjoins a Hadrianic nymphaeum in this exceptionally well-preserved highland city.

vici:vici-24465.label: Agora of Heloros
vici:vici-24465.description: Central agora of Helorus, a Syracusan colony on Sicily's southeast coast founded in the late 8th century BC and surrounded by public buildings; since 2021 the HADES project has documented it via laser scanning and photogrammetry rather than digging.

vici:vici-24502.label: Agora of Bosra
vici:vici-24502.description: Bosra's oval-shaped colonnaded plaza at the western gate, funnelling traffic onto the city's 900m Decumanus Maximus; built largely of local black basalt as Bosra became capital of the Roman province of Arabia after Trajan's 106 CE annexation.

vici:vici-24550.label: Forum
vici:vici-24550.description: The forum of Lousonna, a Gallo-Roman lake-port settlement at Lausanne-Vidy on Lake Geneva; comprises a public square and a 71m basilica dated by excavators to around 40 CE, now part of an archaeological park and Roman museum.

vici:vici-24607.label: Palace of Ugarit [Ugaryt]
vici:vici-24607.description: Royal palace of the kings of Ugarit, a 6,500 m2 complex in the city's northwest corner enclosed by 15th-century BC fortification walls; excavated by Claude Schaeffer from the 1930s, it yielded over 1,000 cuneiform tablets (administrative, legal, diplomatic).
vici:vici-24607.wikidataDescription: ancient palace on the coast of Syria

vici:vici-24611.label: Ugarit [Ugaryt]
vici:vici-24611.description: Bronze Age port city at Ras Shamra that flourished c. 1500-1200 BC as a mercantile kingdom trading with Egypt, Cyprus and the Hittites; excavated since 1929 by Claude Schaeffer, its archives yielded the Ugaritic alphabetic cuneiform script.

vici:vici-24708.label: Royal Palace at Dur Kurigalzu
vici:vici-24708.description: Palace of the Kassite kings at Dur-Kurigalzu, founded by Kurigalzu I in the late 15th/early 14th century BC as the Kassite capital of Babylonia; excavated in 1942-1945 by Taha Baqir and Seton Lloyd alongside the site's famous ziggurat.

vici:vici-24871.label: Aeolian Aigai
vici:vici-24871.description: Aeolian city near Yuntdağı Köseler in Manisa province, member of the Aeolian dodecapolis and a sanctuary of Apollo; flourished under the Attalids of Pergamon and preserves a well-excavated three-storey market building and bouleuterion.
vici:vici-24871.wikidataDescription: ancient city of Aeolis in modern-day Turkey

vici:vici-24876.label: Agora  of Pella. MK
vici:vici-24876.description: The Hellenistic agora of Pella, birthplace of Alexander the Great and capital of Macedon; a vast colonnaded market complex (260 x 238m) spanning ten city blocks, developed under Cassander (316-298 BC) with shops, workshops and administrative rooms.

vici:vici-24928.label: Tusculum
vici:vici-24928.description: Ancient Latin hill city near Frascati in the Alban Hills; its Roman-era forum, theatre and amphitheatre were excavated from 1819-1825, yielding the celebrated 'Tusculum portrait' bust believed to depict Julius Caesar.

vici:vici-25417.label: Mari, Palace of Shakkanakku
vici:vici-25417.description: Earlier palace at Mari built by the shakkanakku military governors who ruled the city after its Akkadian conquest (c. 2300–1900 BC); underlies the later, far larger 260-room royal palace of Zimri-Lim.

vici:vici-25429.label: Zenobia, Governors's House
vici:vici-25429.description: Public building along the Euphrates-facing river wall of Halabiye (ancient Zenobia), the fortress town fortified under Queen Zenobia of Palmyra in the 3rd century AD and refortified by Justinian I in the 6th century; less well preserved than the site's nearby baths and basilicas.

vici:vici-25534.label: Cadianda - Kadyanda
vici:vici-25534.description: Hilltop Lycian city near Üzümlü in the Fethiye district, member of the Lycian League; surviving ruins including a theatre, one-sided stadium, agora, baths and cisterns date mostly to the Roman period; formal excavation began only in 2022.

vici:vici-25579.label: Pergamon, Palace
vici:vici-25579.description: Palace V on the upper acropolis of Pergamon, the probable main residence of the Attalid king Eumenes II (r. 197–159 BC), built around a square peristyle courtyard with an altar, a large hall, and a cistern; part of the royal district excavated since Carl Humann's 1878 campaigns.

vici:vici-25585.label: Pergamon, House of Attalus
vici:vici-25585.description: Peristyle house on the lower acropolis of Pergamon, dated to the 2nd century BC, with a marble mosaic floor, painted walls, and a bathing suite with a small pool; traditionally linked to the Attalid dynasty for whom it is named.

vici:vici-25588.label: Pergamon, Lower Agora
vici:vici-25588.description: Commercial marketplace at the foot of Pergamon's acropolis, built under Eumenes II in the 2nd century BC, measuring about 80 by 55 metres on three terraced levels; fell into disrepair after the 2nd century CE and was later overbuilt with modest houses.

vici:vici-25693.label: Anaktoron of Pantalica
vici:vici-25693.description: Bronze Age megalithic 'palace of the prince' atop the Pantalica plateau in Sicily, built c. 12th–11th century BC of massive blocks with rectangular rooms recalling Mycenaean megara; excavated by Paolo Orsi, who found traces of bronze-working in its largest room.

vici:vici-25741.label: Perachora, West Court
vici:vici-25741.description: Rock-cut polygonal court, roughly 25 x 25m, at the southwest end of the Sanctuary of Hera Akraia near ancient Corinth, sometimes termed the sanctuary's agora; likely dates to the 6th century BC, contemporary with the archaic Temple of Hera Akraia.

vici:vici-25990.label: Balbura, Agora
vici:vici-25990.description: The agora of the Lycian hill-town Balbura (Çölkayiği) had a triple-arched gate on its west side dedicated to Emperor Septimius Severus and his son Geta; the site has only been surveyed, never excavated.

vici:vici-26047.label: Palace at Gla
vici:vici-26047.description: L-shaped 'palace' within the vast Cyclopean-walled Mycenaean citadel of Gla in Boeotia (c. 1300 BC), built after the drainage of Lake Kopais; unusually for a Mycenaean palace it has no throne, central hearth, or Linear B archive.

vici:vici-26223.label: Augusta Emerita, Provincial Forum
vici:vici-26223.description: Excavated from 1980 near the Parador Nacional, this second forum of Augusta Emerita served the imperial cult under Tiberius; its portico bore clipei alternating Jupiter Ammon and Medusa above togate statues of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.

vici:vici-26257.label: Nicopolis of Epirus, Bouleuterion
vici:vici-26257.description: Council house of Nicopolis, the 'Victory City' Octavian founded in 29 BC on the Epirus promontory across from Actium to commemorate his defeat of Antony and Cleopatra; part of the Augustan public-building program.

vici:vici-26639.label: Lower Agora, Xanthos
vici:vici-26639.description: One of two public squares at Xanthos, ancient capital of Lycia, sited in the lower town near later Byzantine churches and distinct from the later Roman agora built near the theatre and dedicated to the Twelve Lycian Gods.

vici:vici-26647.label: Forum of Andriake [Andriace]
vici:vici-26647.description: Andriake, the harbour town of Myra, had a market and forum among its restored port installations alongside a 5th-century synagogue and Hadrian's great grain warehouse; the port thrived on the Egypt-to-Rome grain trade under Hadrian.

vici:vici-26654.label: Agora of Adada
vici:vici-26654.description: The agora of Adada, a fortified Pisidian hill-city, is reached by a monumental staircase and stands near the city's theatre and its imperial-cult temples, including one to Trajan built before c. 110-114 CE.

vici:vici-26657.label: Adada, Roman Forum
vici:vici-26657.description: Roman civic square of Adada, a Pisidian hill-town that minted its own coinage and flourished under Trajan, Hadrian, and Antoninus Pius; the site preserves several temples to the emperors, including Trajan and Zeus-Serapis jointly.

vici:vici-26677.label: Agora of Philippi
vici:vici-26677.description: Roman forum of Philippi, built in phases from Claudius to Antoninus Pius east of the earlier Greek agora; held temples, a basilica, a library, and the bema traditionally identified as where Paul and Silas were flogged (Acts 16).

vici:vici-26816.label: Kremna, Forum of Longus
vici:vici-26816.description: Forum and basilica of the Roman colony of Cremna were funded by L. Fabricius Longus, priest of the colony's Fortuna cult; the basilica, dedicated c. AD 120, honored Trajan, Hadrian, and the imperial house.

vici:vici-27508.label: Palace of Ctesiphon
vici:vici-27508.description: Taq Kasra, the vaulted audience-hall façade of the Sasanian royal palace at Ctesiphon, built between the 3rd and 6th centuries AD; its brick iwan, rising 37m, is the largest unreinforced brick vault surviving from antiquity, captured by the Arabs in 637.
vici:vici-27508.wikidataDescription: Sassanid-era Persian monument in modern Iraq

vici:vici-27717.label: Dur Untash, Palace
vici:vici-27717.description: Royal palace in the outer precinct of Dur-Untash (Chogha Zanbil), the Elamite religious city built c. 1250 BC by king Untash-Napirisha around a great ziggurat; the outer precinct also held a subterranean funerary palace with five royal tombs.

vici:vici-27722.label: Dur Untash, Palace I
vici:vici-27722.description: The 'hypogeum palace' at Dur-Untash (Chogha Zanbil), built by Untash-Napirisha c. 1250 BC; its five vaulted underground burial chambers each held one skeleton beside cremated remains, and the site stayed in ritual use until c. 1000 BC.

vici:vici-27754.label: Ehursag, Ur [Urim]
vici:vici-27754.description: Built by Ur-Nammu and completed under Shulgi (c. 2100-2050 BC) at Ur, this 59-metre-square, 41-room brick building was excavated by Leonard Woolley, who identified it as the Third Dynasty royal palace, though its function remains debated.

vici:vici-27797.label: Ur [Urim], Palace of Bel-Shalti Nannar
vici:vici-27797.description: Residence of Ennigaldi (Bel-Shalti-Nannar), high priestess of Ur and daughter of King Nabonidus, who around 530 BC assembled here what is considered history's oldest known museum, cataloguing older Mesopotamian antiquities; excavated by Leonard Woolley in 1925.
vici:vici-27797.wikidataDescription: museum in Ur, thought to be the first by some historians

vici:vici-27812.label: Palace of Sin-Kashid, Uruk [Warka]
vici:vici-27812.description: Built c. 19th century BC by Sin-kashid, founder of a new Amorite dynasty at Uruk, this roughly 142x110-metre palace held audience halls, storerooms and residential quarters; excavated by the German Archaeological Institute and reconstructed for a 2013-14 Berlin exhibition.

vici:vici-27829.label: Kish
vici:vici-27829.description: Kish's Palace A ('Palace of the Kings'), an Early Dynastic III complex near the Ishtar temple, is known for rare columned porticoes and shell-and-limestone inlay plaques of bound captives; excavated 1923-33 by Oxford University and Chicago's Field Museum under Stephen Langdon.

vici:vici-27844.label: Governor's Palace, Nimrud
vici:vici-27844.description: Excavated by Max Mallowan in 1949-50 at Nimrud, this administrative building yielded some 230 cuneiform tablets recording the activities of Assyrian provincial governors, plus a cache of fine ceramics nicknamed the 'governor's dinner service'.

vici:vici-27977.label: Agora of Cnidus [Knidos]
vici:vici-27977.description: The agora lay among Knidos's public buildings first investigated by C. T. Newton's 1857-58 mission for the British Museum; systematic Turkish excavations, led by Ertekin Doksanaltı since 2012, continue to uncover the site.

vici:vici-28302.label: Iader forum
vici:vici-28302.description: The largest Roman forum on the Adriatic's eastern shore (c. 95x45 m), built under Augustus and completed per two 3rd-century dedicatory inscriptions; framed by porticoes and tabernae, with a Capitolium temple to Jupiter, Juno and Minerva.

vici:vici-28813.label: Agora of Nysa ad Meandrum
vici:vici-28813.description: Excavations of Nysa's agora recovered a 1998 inscription honoring the Roman procurator Domitius Philippus (3rd century AD); the colonnaded Roman-era plaza remains under investigation by University of Ankara/Aydın Museum teams active since 1990.

vici:vici-28890.label: Sarıkaya Palace, Acemhoyuk
vici:vici-28890.description: A two-storey, roughly 50-room palace at Acemhöyük dating to the 18th century BC, the largest known Bronze Age building in Anatolia; sealed bullae found here link it to Assyrian, Mari and Karkemish rulers, alongside ivory, gold and lapis-lazuli luxury goods.

vici:vici-28913.label: Notion [Notium], East Agora
vici:vici-28913.description: University of Michigan-led excavations begun in 2022 focused on the Bouleuterion on the agora's east side, opposite a peristyle courtyard house on the west; work continued through 2024 at this Ionian port city near Colophon.

vici:vici-28918.label: Praetorium Biesheim
vici:vici-28918.description: Part of the Roman frontier settlement of Argentovaria (Oedenburg) on the Rhine near Colmar; this late-antique roadside praetorium and an adjoining fortified palace mark reinforcement of Rhine defenses against Alemannic incursions, explored since 1998 by joint French-German-Swiss excavations.

vici:vici-29000.label: Praetorium valentinien
vici:vici-29000.description: Representative administrative and residential building within the late Roman fort on Breisach's Münsterberg (Mons Brisiacus); Emperor Valentinian I stayed here in 369 CE while directing fortification of the Upper Rhine frontier, issuing an imperial rescript on 30 August that year.

vici:vici-29002.label: Macellum Aguntum (Lienz)
vici:vici-29002.description: Excavated in 2006, this circular market hall on the forum of Aguntum is one of only five known Roman circular macella in Europe, combining a square outline with an inner decagon; it traded fish, oysters and other delicacies.

vici:vici-29008.label: Samaria - Sebastia, Roman Forum
vici:vici-29008.description: Part of Herod the Great's rebuilding of Samaria as Sebaste (renamed c. 27 BC to honor Augustus), the forum adjoined a large basilica used for judicial and civic business, part of a building program that also included a stadium and aqueduct.

vici:vici-29144.label: Agora of Perge
vici:vici-29144.description: A square plaza (65 m per side) surrounded by colonnaded shops, some with mosaic floors; a central circular structure, comparable to the Tyche temple at Side, is thought to have served as a fountain rather than a shrine.

vici:vici-29256.label: Agora of Pamphylian Seleucia - Lybre
vici:vici-29256.description: Hellenistic-period agora at Lyrbe (often mislabeled as Pamphylian Seleucia), renovated under Rome and again in early Byzantine times; considered the best-preserved agora in ancient Pamphylia, near Bucakşeyhler in southern Turkey.
vici:vici-29256.wikidataDescription: ancient city of Pamphylia in modern-day Turkey

vici:vici-29276.label: Ebla, The Western Palace Q
vici:vici-29276.description: Middle Bronze Age palace (Area Q) west of Ebla's acropolis, built as the residence of the reigning crown prince; a seal naming Prince Maratewari was recovered here alongside the associated royal necropolis of the Amorite period.

vici:vici-29288.label: Ebla, Palace P5
vici:vici-29288.description: Archaic royal palace built in Ebla's lower town northwest of the acropolis during the city's Second Kingdom (Middle Bronze I, c. 2000 BCE); it was later replaced by the so-called Intermediate Palace.

vici:vici-30339.label: Behistun, throne hall
vici:vici-30339.description: The domed audience hall of Shapur I's palace at Bishapur, built after 260 CE partly using Roman labor following the capture of Emperor Valerian; its cross-shaped plan with four iwans around a domed square was an early landmark of Sasanian architecture.

vici:vici-30631.label: Selcuk Palace
vici:vici-30631.description: Two-storey palace around a central courtyard on a cliff above Ani's Bostanlar creek, dated stylistically to the 12th-13th centuries; also called the Palace of the Pahlavuni or the Baron's Palace, its function debated between princely residence and barracks.

vici:vici-30632.label: Citadel & Palace
vici:vici-30632.description: Two-storey palace built around a courtyard within the walled citadel (Iç Kale) at Ani, on a promontory fortified since the 7th century; it served as the residence of the Bagratid kings of Ani and, before them, possibly the Kamsarakan princes.

vici:vici-31615.label: Lower Palace
vici:vici-31615.description: The Lower Palace area of Carchemish, containing the Great Staircase, King's Gate, and Temple of the Storm God; excavated by Woolley (1911–1920) and by Turco-Italian teams since 2011, which found a Late Bronze Age monumental building here in 2017.

vici:vici-31867.label: Achaemenid palace
vici:vici-31867.description: Charkhab Palace near Borazjan, a 45×35m hypostyle hall complex built under Cyrus the Great (mid-6th century BC) with later Darius I-era additions; excavated since the 1970s, its administration is attested in the Persepolis Fortification tablets.
vici:vici-31867.wikidataDescription: palace in Dashtestan County, Iranian national heritage site

vici:vici-31878.label: Behistun, unfinished Sasanian palace
vici:vici-31878.description: An unfinished palace begun by Sasanian king Khosrow II (r. 590–628) as part of a planned complex with a giant cliff relief and bridge commemorating his Byzantine campaigns; abandoned after his 628 assassination and later converted into a caravanserai.
vici:vici-31878.wikidataDescription: caravanserai in Bisotun, Iranian national heritage site

vici:vici-31908.label: Balkuwara Palace Complex (Abbasid era)
vici:vici-31908.description: A fortified Abbasid palace on the Tigris south of Samarra, roughly 1,170m per side, built 849–859 for prince al-Mu'tazz under his father Caliph al-Mutawakkil, with three courtyards, nine halls, and stucco, mosaic, and painted decoration.

vici:vici-31909.label: Jawsaq al-Khaqani, the Caliphal Palace
vici:vici-31909.description: The Caliphal Palace (Dar al-Khilafa) at Samarra, begun around 836 by Caliph al-Mu'tasim as his private residence within a 180,000m2 walled complex that also housed the public Dar al-'Amma audience hall; main Abbasid seat until the court returned to Baghdad in 892.

vici:vici-31910.label: Ruins of Haruni Palace
vici:vici-31910.description: Palace built on the Tigris at Samarra by Caliph al-Wathiq (given name Harun) around 842–847; used by his successor al-Mutawakkil as residence until 859, and usually identified with the flood-affected riverside site of al-Quwair.

vici:vici-32183.label: Shadikanni Palace
vici:vici-32183.description: Palace of Shadikanni (Tell Ajaja), a Neo-Assyrian provincial capital on the Khabur River; 1982 excavations found a lamassu inscribed with the name of governor Mushezib-Ninurta and a winged bull in situ flanking a monumental building's entrance.

vici:vici-32730.label: Antiochia Pisidiae, Agora
vici:vici-32730.description: Agora of Antioch in Pisidia (Yalvaç, Turkey), a Roman colonia refounded by Augustus around 25 BC; excavated since 1924, first by a University of Michigan team led by Ramsay, Kelsey and Robinson.

vici:vici-33399.label: Tell Arad, Palace
vici:vici-33399.description: The Early Bronze II palace of Tel Arad's fortified lower city (c. 3000–2650 BC), a large complex of interconnected rooms, courtyards, and storage areas between the western gate and the reservoir; excavated by Ruth Amiran from 1962–1984.

vici:vici-34191.label: Northeast Palace (Tal Halaf)
vici:vici-34191.description: Neo-Assyrian governor's palace built at Tell Halaf (ancient Guzana) after Assyria absorbed the Aramaean kingdom of Bit-Bahiani in the 9th century BC; excavated with the site's famous orthostat reliefs by Max von Oppenheim from 1911.

vici:vici-34193.label: West Palace (Hilani) (Tal Halaf)
vici:vici-34193.description: Bit-hilani palace built by King Kapara of Bit-Bahiani at Tell Halaf (Guzana), 10th–9th century BC; flanked by scorpion-man gate figures and orthostat reliefs, its statues were shattered in the 1943 Berlin bombing and reassembled from 27,000 fragments.

vici:vici-34652.label: Mallia, Polythyron
vici:vici-34652.description: A polythyron (pier-and-door partition hall) within the Bronze Age Minoan palace of Malia, Crete, whose removable door leaves let rooms be opened or sealed for light, air, and ceremony; palace flourished c. 1900-1450 BC.

vici:vici-34843.label: Thera, Agora
vici:vici-34843.description: Agora of ancient Thera on Mesa Vouno, Santorini, excavated 1895-1904 by Friedrich Hiller von Gaertringen alongside the city's theatre and over 200 early Greek inscriptions documenting civic life.

vici:vici-35235.label: Khan Omurtag Palace
vici:vici-35235.description: Stone palace and fort built for the Bulgar ruler Omurtag in 822 AD near Han Krum, Shumen Province, replacing an earlier 8th-century timber fortress; its construction is recorded in the Chatalar Inscription.

vici:vici-36037.label: Felix Romuliana, Palace Complex
vici:vici-36037.description: Imperial palace built by Emperor Galerius at Gamzigrad (Felix Romuliana), Serbia, from c. 298 AD and named for his mother Romula; a fortified tetrarchic residence with porticoed halls, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

vici:vici-37433.label: Herod's Third Palace, Jericho
vici:vici-37433.description: The largest and most elaborate of Herod the Great's Jericho palaces, built c. 15 BCE spanning both banks of Wadi Qelt with a sunken garden, artificial pool, and opus reticulatum masonry; excavated by Ehud Netzer from 1973.

vici:vici-37434.label: Herod's second Palace, Jericho
vici:vici-37434.description: Built by Herod the Great c. 30 BCE atop the ruins of an earthquake-destroyed Hasmonean palace north of Wadi Qelt, with a large pool, bathhouse and gardens; excavated by Ehud Netzer after 1973.

vici:vici-37592.label: Susa, Palace of Darius I the Great
vici:vici-37592.description: Darius I's winter palace at Susa, begun c. 521 BCE; his own foundation inscription describes materials and craftsmen drawn from across the empire—cedar from Lebanon, gold from Sardis, ivory from Nubia. First excavated by Marcel Dieulafoy in the 1880s.

vici:vici-39044.label: Persepolis, Queen's Quarters
vici:vici-39044.description: Built under Xerxes I as the residence of the royal women (the 'harem'), west of the Treasury at Persepolis; its restored facade has housed the Persepolis Museum since the 1930s excavations.

vici:vici-39107.label: Persepolis, Hall of the Thirty-Two Columns
vici:vici-39107.description: A columned hall added to Persepolis under Artaxerxes III (r. 358–338 BCE), one of the palace complex's last major building phases before Alexander's sack in 330 BCE; its exact function is unknown.

vici:vici-39637.label: Utica, Forum
vici:vici-39637.description: Forum of Roman Utica in Tunisia, an unusually large complex ringed by temples and administrative buildings; excavated from the 19th century onward, with recent seasons run by the Tunisian-British Utica Project.

vici:vici-39920.label: Baelo Claudia, Forum
vici:vici-39920.description: Forum of Baelo Claudia (Bolonia, Spain), the only fully excavated Roman forum in Hispania; the surviving remains were rebuilt under Claudius-Nero (AD 50-70) and face a capitolium with temples to Jupiter, Juno and Minerva.

vici:vici-40791.label: Khirbet al-Batrawy, Palace of the Copper Axes
vici:vici-40791.description: An Early Bronze Age III (c. 2500–2300 BCE) palace at this fortified Jordanian town, excavated by Lorenzo Nigro's Sapienza University mission since 2005; named for a hoard of five ceremonial copper axes found in its hall in 2010–11.

vici:vici-41106.label: Urkesh, Palace
vici:vici-41106.description: Royal palace of the Hurrian king Tupkish and queen Uqnitum at Urkesh, built c. 2300 BCE; seal impressions from its archive document the royal court, including links to Naram-Sin of Akkad. Only the service wing has been excavated.

vici:vici-41110.label: Tell Brak, Mitannian palace
vici:vici-41110.description: A late 2nd-millennium BCE Mitanni palace and temple complex of distinctive red mudbrick atop Tell Brak's highest mound, excavated in 1985–87; storerooms yielded evidence of glass and metal (copper and iron) working.

vici:vici-41118.label: Tell Leilan, Qarni-Lim Palace
vici:vici-41118.description: Palace built by Qarni-Lim, king of Andarig, at Šubat-Enlil (Tell Leilan) around 1770 BC as a de facto embassy during his political dominance over local rulers Zuzu and Ḫaya-abum; excavated 1991, yielding over 600 cuneiform tablets, mostly a 'beer archive'.

vici:vici-41119.label: Tell Leilan, Šamšī-Adad Palace
vici:vici-41119.description: Royal palace at Šubat-Enlil (Tell Leilan), the city Šamši-Adad I made his capital and residence during his conquest of Upper Mesopotamia in the early 18th century BC; partially excavated by Harvey Weiss's Yale expedition.

vici:vici-41219.label: Paphos, agora
vici:vici-41219.description: Hellenistic-Roman agora of Nea Paphos, Cyprus, excavated since 2011 by the Jagiellonian University's Paphos Agora Project; finds include a bronze weight naming the agoranomos Seleucus and hundreds of Hellenistic-era coins.

vici:vici-41728.label: Salamis, Agora [Cyprus]
vici:vici-41728.description: Agora/forum of Salamis, Cyprus, roughly 230 by 55 metres with shop-lined stoas along its long sides, among the largest known from antiquity; Hellenistic in origin, restored under Augustus around 22 BC.

vici:vici-42277.label: Kumidi, Palace
vici:vici-42277.description: Late Bronze Age palace at Kumidi (Kamid el-Loz, Lebanon), seat of the Egyptian governor overseeing the southern Levant under pharaohs Amenhotep III and Akhenaten; the city and its officials, including governor Puhuru, appear repeatedly in the Amarna letters.

vici:vici-42772.label: Forum
vici:vici-42772.description: Forum of Carnuntum, the Roman legionary fortress and later capital of Pannonia Superior on the Danube (Petronell-Carnuntum/Bad Deutsch-Altenburg, Austria); it lay within the civilian town, now part of the Carnuntum Archaeological Park.

vici:vici-42899.label: Forum des Caesars
vici:vici-42899.description: Built by Julius Caesar and dedicated in 46 BC as Rome's first purpose-built imperial forum, centred on the Temple of Venus Genetrix honouring his claimed ancestress; completed and later enlarged by Trajan.

vici:vici-42990.label: Forum
vici:vici-42990.description: The civic forum of Roman Gnathia (Egnazia) on the Adriatic coast, flanked by porticoes, a basilica and a sanctuary; excavation of the site began in 1912 and continues today.

vici:vici-43050.label: Dvin, Palace of the Katholikos
vici:vici-43050.description: Seat of the Armenian Catholicos at Dvin, an early 7th-century complex centered on a colonnaded hall over 26 m long with carved capitals; a key monument of early medieval Armenian civil architecture, ruined by a catastrophic earthquake in the late 9th century.

vici:vici-43076.label: Macellum
vici:vici-43076.description: The macellum (covered market) of Aquincum's civil town, built in the mid-3rd century AD with a colonnaded courtyard and a central round tholos, its plan echoing North African market halls.

vici:vici-43079.label: Forum
vici:vici-43079.description: The forum of the civilian town of Aquincum (Roman Budapest), the administrative and market centre of the municipium/colonia, built with a large temple and assembly hall within the walled town founded c. AD 124.

vici:vici-43105.label: Forum
vici:vici-43105.description: The forum and basilica of Cambodunum (Kempten), first capital of the Roman province of Raetia, rebuilt in stone after a fire destroyed the largely timber town in AD 69.

vici:vici-43106.label: Prätorium
vici:vici-43106.description: Governor's residence of the Roman province of Raetia at Cambodunum (Kempten), later converted into a guest house as the town's political importance declined; its foundations, with an attached bath, are reconstructed in the Archäologischer Park Cambodunum.

vici:vici-43137.label: Forum
vici:vici-43137.description: The forum of Roman Avennio (Avignon), sited beneath today's Place de l'Horloge; almost nothing survives above ground beyond fragmentary arches reused in later buildings, unlike the better-preserved forums of Orange or Vaison.

vici:vici-43160.label: Praetorium
vici:vici-43160.description: Reconstructed commander's residence of the Saalburg fort on the Upper Germanic Limes, rebuilt 1897–1907 under Kaiser Wilhelm II and again from 2004 to reflect updated archaeological evidence; now houses the fort's research institute and administration.

vici:vici-4357.label: Forum in park Arentsburg
vici:vici-4357.description: Forum Hadriani, the Cananefates' market town named for Hadrian's visit c. AD 121-122, was the northernmost Roman town on the continent; its remains lie under Voorburg's Arentsburg park, first excavated in 1827-1834 by Caspar Reuvens in the Netherlands' first systematic archaeological dig.

vici:vici-43592.label: Side, Bishop`s Palace
vici:vici-43592.description: Byzantine-era bishop's palace at Side, built in the 5th–6th centuries beside the city's basilica cathedral when Side, seat of the bishopric of Eastern Pamphylia, briefly revived as an ecclesiastical center.

vici:vici-44250.label: Butrint-Bouthroton Triconch Palace
vici:vici-44250.description: Elite late-Roman house at Butrint remodeled around 420–425 AD with a three-apsed (triconch) dining hall and a private pier for waterborne guests; abandoned mid-construction, its floors unpaved and walls unplastered, likely due to rising lake levels.

vici:vici-44811.label: Forum
vici:vici-44811.description: The forum of Aregenua (Vieux-la-Romaine), chief town of the Gallic Viducasses near Caen, built in the early 2nd century AD with a curia fitted with a lavishly decorated tiered hemicycle.

vici:vici-45216.label: Forum
vici:vici-45216.description: Forum of Ercávica, a Celtiberian oppidum near Cañaveruelas (Cuenca) that became a Roman municipium under Augustus; a paved rectangular plaza ringed by porticoes, basilica and shops, fully excavated from 1972 onward.

vici:vici-46797.label: Midea, Palace on the lower  acropolis
vici:vici-46797.description: Megaron-form palace complex on Midea's lower acropolis terraces, built in the Mycenaean palatial period (LH IIIB2) and destroyed by fire around 1200 BC along with the rest of the citadel, then rebuilt on a smaller scale with a central colonnade in LH IIIC.

vici:vici-50161.label: Forum romain
vici:vici-50161.description: Forum of Apta Julia (modern Apt), founded on Julius Caesar's order in 45 BC as a colony on the Via Domitia; excavations beneath the town revealed the forum, a basilica, and the decumanus and cardo maximus.

vici:vici-50642.label: Governors Palace
vici:vici-50642.description: The roughly seven-hectare residence of the governor of Pannonia Inferior on Óbuda's Hajógyári-sziget island near Aquincum, first built under Hadrian in the 2nd century AD with mosaic floors and underfloor heating, rebuilt after a fire in the early 3rd century, and abandoned by the late 3rd century.

vici:vici-52210.label: Tell Abu Shijar
vici:vici-52210.description: A mound within the Kassite capital of Dur-Kurigalzu near Baghdad; Iraqi excavations in 1992, 1993 and 2001 uncovered Late Kassite and Parthian-Sasanian remains, painted wall plaster, a cylinder seal, and cuneiform tablets dated to king Nazi-Maruttash.

vici:vici-52622.label: Thessaloniki, Greek Agora
vici:vici-52622.description: Roman Forum of Thessaloniki, a two-terraced complex with double-storey stoas, baths and a small theatre used for gladiatorial games; found by accident in the 1960s, excavated in the 1970s-80s, and used into the 6th century.

vici:vici-52625.label: Palaiopolis, Agora
vici:vici-52625.description: Agora of ancient Korkyra at Palaiopolis, Corfu, excavated 1936-1955 alongside the Early Christian basilica of Agia Kerkyra; the settlement was founded by Corinthian colonists (led by Chersicrates) in the 8th century BC.

vici:vici-53620.label: Foro de Segobriga
vici:vici-53620.description: Forum of Segóbriga, built c. 15 BC under Augustus and partly funded by Proculus Spantamicus, whose name in bronze letters fronted a monument bearing the emperor's statue; a rectangular plaza framed by a colonnaded portico.

vici:vici-53629.label: Foro de Valeria
vici:vici-53629.description: Forum of Valeria, among the best-preserved on the Iberian Meseta, built mainly in the 1st century AD with a basilica, curia/exedra, cryptoporticus, monumental staircase, shops and the roughly 100m-long nymphaeum fountain.

vici:vici-53785.label: Foro de Complutum
vici:vici-53785.description: Forum of Complutum (Alcalá de Henares): a monumental 3rd-century complex with basilica, curia, baths and porticoed shops (tabernae), built over an earlier 1st-century forum; the city flourished until the 6th-7th century.

vici:vici-54676.label: Bishapur, Palace, Mosaic hall
vici:vici-54676.description: Cross-shaped reception hall at the core of Shapur I's palace at Bishapur, flanked by 'mosaic halls' whose Sasanian floor mosaics of banqueting, dancing and portrait figures show Roman artistic influence; excavated by Roman Ghirshman for the Louvre, 1935-1941.

vici:vici-54715.label: Persepolis, Unexcavated Palace "D"
vici:vici-54715.description: A largely unexcavated Achaemenid structure east of the Palace of Xerxes at Persepolis, known chiefly from scattered relief fragments (including a small winged-monster relief) and never fully cleared or published.

vici:vici-54817.label: Dura Europos, Redoubt Palace
vici:vici-54817.description: Hellenistic palace of Dura-Europos's military governor (the strategos), built within a fortified 'redoubt' on high ground above the Euphrates in the 2nd century BC; its state rooms open onto a colonnaded courtyard about 11 by 11.5 metres, with the Temple of Zeus Megistos immediately to the south.

vici:vici-54922.label: Glanum, Forum
vici:vici-54922.description: Civic square of Glanum, a Gallo-Greek/Gallo-Roman town below the Alpilles that grew from a Celtic sanctuary to the healing spring-god Glanis; monumentalized under Augustus, excavated from 1921, abandoned after 3rd-century raids.

vici:vici-55005.label: Umayri Palace
vici:vici-55005.description: A well-preserved Late Bronze Age building at Tall al-'Umayri excavated by the Madaba Plains Project, first called a 'palace' but reinterpreted as a temple after standing stones, chalices, lamps and figurines were found; its walls survive over three metres high.

vici:vici-55083.label: Garni, Palace of Tiridates
vici:vici-55083.description: Summer residence of the Arsacid kings of Armenia within the Garni fortress, built under Tiridates I in the 1st century CE; its bath house preserves a Greek-inscribed mosaic of Oceanus and Thetis, the only pagan-era mosaic to survive in Armenia.

vici:vici-55151.label: Lepcis Magna, Old Forum
vici:vici-55151.description: Leptis Magna's original forum (Forum Vetus), predating the later Severan Forum, flanked by temples to Liber Pater, Rome and Augustus (built 8 BC-19 AD), and Hercules — a key monument of the city's Augustan-era Romanization.

vici:vici-55156.label: Amman, Forum
vici:vici-55156.description: Forum of Roman Philadelphia (Amman), one of the largest public squares of the Roman world at roughly 100 x 50 m, built in the 2nd century AD facing the Roman theatre and bounded by the Seil Amman stream.

vici:vici-55220.label: Petra, Upper Market
vici:vici-55220.description: Upper terrace above Petra's colonnaded street, reached by a monumental staircase past a Trajanic-period arch; part of the city's Nabataean-to-Roman civic/commercial core, in use from the 1st century BC into the 7th century AD.

vici:vici-55287.label: Heraclea Lyncestis, Episcopal Palace
vici:vici-55287.description: Bishop's residence at Heraclea Lyncestis, excavated 1970–75; its four private chambers, floored with Early Christian figural mosaics, formed part of the early Byzantine episcopal complex alongside the Great Basilica.

vici:vici-55320.label: Susa, Achaemenid Palace, Third Court
vici:vici-55320.description: The outermost of three courtyards in Darius I's palace at Susa, begun c. 510 BCE and excavated by Jane and Marcel Dieulafoy in the 1880s, part of the residential quarter west of the famous Apadana.

vici:vici-55321.label: Susa, Achaemenid Palace, Second Court
vici:vici-55321.description: Central courtyard of Darius I's Susa palace, where archaeologists dug through into pre-Achaemenid occupation levels beneath the Persian remains during 19th–20th century excavations.

vici:vici-55322.label: Susa, Achaemenid Palace, First Court
vici:vici-55322.description: Innermost courtyard of the Susa palace, often identified with the 'inner court' before the king's gate in the biblical Book of Esther, giving access to the King's Hall.

vici:vici-55323.label: Susa, Achaemenid Palace, Throne Room
vici:vici-55323.description: The king's audience chamber south of the palace courtyards at Susa, where Darius I and his successors received visitors on the royal throne; excavated with the adjoining Apadana in the 1880s–1900s.

vici:vici-55721.label: Meroe, Royal Palace
vici:vici-55721.description: The main royal palace (Building M 750) of the Kushite capital at Meroë, excavated by John Garstang in the early 20th century and again in 2004–2007, revealing courtyard architecture and an earlier mudbrick palace beneath dating to c. 900 BCE.

vici:vici-55798.label: Provincial forum
vici:vici-55798.description: The Provincial Forum of Tarraco, seat of the imperial cult and assembly of Hispania Citerior, built from 73 AD under Vespasian on two terraces, its lower square measuring about 318 x 175 m; part of the UNESCO-listed Tarraco ensemble.

vici:vici-56005.label: Ur, E-gipar
vici:vici-56005.description: Residence of the entu-priestess of the moon god Nanna at Ur; excavated by Leonard Woolley in 1927, it yielded the alabaster disk of Enheduanna, priestess-daughter of Sargon of Akkad and history's earliest named author.

vici:vici-56023.label: Kourion, Episcopal Palace
vici:vici-56023.description: Part of Kourion's fifth-century Episcopal precinct, seat of the city's Christian bishop alongside its basilica and baptistery; excavated in the 1930s-70s. Occupation ended after Arab raids destroyed the site in 649.

vici:vici-56024.label: Kourion, Roman Agora
vici:vici-56024.description: Agora of Kourion, rebuilt in the late 2nd-early 3rd century AD over an earlier Hellenistic public building, ringed by marble-columned porticoes and giving access to a large nymphaeum and bath complex on its northwest side.

vici:vici-56141.label: Criptopórtico (forum)
vici:vici-56141.description: The cryptoporticus of Aeminium (Coimbra): a 1st/2nd-century AD underground gallery of vaulted corridors built to level the site for the city's forum, preserved intact beneath the Bishop's Palace, today the Machado de Castro National Museum.

vici:vici-57411.label: Market
vici:vici-57411.description: Marketplace of Porolissum's civilian settlement, a Dacian frontier town and customs station on the Roman limes; excavations there recovered coins, native brooches, and raw Baltic amber marking a branch of the Amber Road into the empire.

vici:vici-58125.label: Imperial Palace
vici:vici-58125.description: The 'Palazzo Imperiale' at Portus, a three-storey imperial residence of nearly 7.5 acres built late under Trajan or early under Hadrian between the Claudian and Trajanic harbour basins, likely used by the port's procurator and visiting emperors.

vici:vici-58131.label: Market
vici:vici-58131.description: A market building within Portus, the artificial harbour Claudius built for Rome's grain supply near Ostia and Trajan later enlarged with a hexagonal inner basin and vast warehouse complex.

vici:vici-58497.label: Tiberian Palace
vici:vici-58497.description: The Domus Tiberiana on the Palatine's northwest slope, begun under Tiberius and enlarged by his successors; damaged in the 64 AD fire, absorbed into Nero's Domus Aurea, and later the Antonine emperors' main residence.
vici:vici-58497.wikidataDescription: Imperial Roman palace in ancient Rome, located on the northwest corner of the Palatine Hill

vici:vici-58751.label: Imperial Palace
vici:vici-58751.description: The so-called 'Palazzo Imperiale' in Ostia's Regio I, a multi-purpose complex of baths, shops and a mithraeum built mainly under the Antonine and Severan emperors; a lead pipe naming Trajan's niece Matidia ties it to the imperial family, not an emperor's own residence.

vici:vici-60162.label: Forum
vici:vici-60162.description: The forum of Augusta Bagiennorum, chief town of the Ligurian Bagienni founded near the end of the 1st century BC; excavated in 1941, it revealed a paved square 36 by 116 m flanked by porticoes with shop and office rooms.

vici:vici-60813.label: Forum
vici:vici-60813.description: The forum of Virunum, capital of the Roman province of Noricum founded under Claudius on the Zollfeld plain; it lay toward the eastern end of the grid, flanked by a Capitolium and enclosed on three sides by a double colonnade.

vici:vici-60834.label: Praetorium
vici:vici-60834.description: The commander's residence within the 23-hectare Roman legionary camp at Anreppen on the Lippe, built around AD 4 for Tiberius's Germanic campaigns; at roughly 3,400 m2 it was the largest praetorium of the Lippe camps, abandoned by AD 9.

vici:vici-61062.label: Roman Governor’s Palace
vici:vici-61062.description: Part of the Ruin Garden at Savaria (Szombathely), capital of Pannonia Superior, excavated from 1932; its mosaic-paved remains are traditionally identified as the governor's palace, where visiting emperors including Septimius Severus reportedly stayed.

vici:vici-61066.label: Imperial palace
vici:vici-61066.description: At Salla (Zalalövő) on the Amber Road, a Roman camp founded in the early 1st century AD grew into a municipium under Hadrian in 124; in the early 4th century its site was rebuilt in stone as a guest house for high-status travelers.

vici:vici-61516.label: Forum
vici:vici-61516.description: The forum of Gigthis, a Phoenician-founded trading post on Tunisia's Gulf of Gabès that became a Roman municipium under Antoninus Pius; a colonnaded, limestone-paved esplanade fronting a temple, at its height in the 2nd–3rd centuries CE.

vici:vici-62327.label: Palatial Complex
vici:vici-62327.description: The 'Palatial Complex' at Kerkenes Dağ, entered through a monumental gateway in the 7 km circuit wall of this Iron Age Anatolian city, the largest pre-Hellenistic settlement on the plateau; built and occupied for about a century before its destruction c. 550 BC.

vici:vici-62664.label: Forum
vici:vici-62664.description: The forum of Althiburos (Henchir Medeina), a Berber-Numidian settlement that became a Roman municipium under Hadrian; excavations from 1908 uncovered the forum, a main street, and a monumental gate inscribed to Hadrian.

vici:vici-63346.label: Palace of the Porphyrogenitus
vici:vici-63346.description: Late 13th-century Byzantine palace built for co-emperor Constantine Palaiologos as an annex of the Blachernae complex; the best-preserved of Constantinople's three surviving Byzantine palaces, later used as an Ottoman menagerie, pottery workshop and Jewish poorhouse.

vici:vici-63435.label: Praetorium
vici:vici-63435.description: The 'Praetorium' at Umm el-Jimal, a Roman military headquarters built around AD 180 and named by excavator H. C. Butler in 1905; its cross-shaped domed hall was later remodeled into a luxurious Umayyad dwelling with mosaics and frescoes.

vici:vici-63782.label: Palazzo d’Attila
vici:vici-63782.description: A large Roman maritime villa near the Timavo river's mouth at Duino, popularly but wrongly linked to Attila; its terraced concrete substructure, over 35 metres long, overcomes a 10-metre drop toward the sea using techniques paralleling Campanian and Latial villas.

vici:vici-63970.label: Rome, Comitium
vici:vici-63970.description: The Comitium, Rome's original open-air assembly and law-court space beside the Senate house; excavations by Giacomo Boni in 1899–1903 uncovered the Lapis Niger, an Old Latin inscription of c. 570–550 BC among the earliest known.
vici:vici-63970.wikidataDescription: original open-air public meeting space of Ancient Rome

vici:vici-65731.label: Forum e acrópole da Torre d'Aires
vici:vici-65731.description: Forum of the Roman Lusitanian port city of Balsa, sited on the hill at Quinta da Torre d'Aires; despite Balsa's size, its urban core and forum remained undocumented until geophysical prospection and excavations finally located them in 2019.

vici:vici-67664.label: Kaisariye in Saccaea
vici:vici-67664.description: The ruined governor's palace ('Kaisariye', imperial residence) of Saccaea, renamed Maximianopolis in AD 287; built in dark basalt around the mid-3rd century with a domed reception hall and niched corridors, remaining in use into the Byzantine period.

vici:vici-67760.label: Khirbet el-Mafjar
vici:vici-67760.description: Lavish early 8th-century Umayyad desert palace and bath complex near Jericho, likely begun under Caliph Hisham; its bathhouse floor bears the 'Tree of Life' mosaic, one of the largest and finest figural mosaics surviving from the Islamic world.
vici:vici-67760.wikidataDescription: archaeological site in the West Bank

vici:vici-67778.label: Babisqa [Babiska]
vici:vici-67778.description: Marketplace at Babisqa, a Byzantine-era village in Syria's 'Dead Cities'; a portico inscription dates the 33 m, five-chamber, two-storey arcaded structure to 547 CE, alongside two churches and the region's only certain public baths.

vici:vici-69282.label: Kubadabad Palace
vici:vici-69282.description: Seljuk summer palace complex of Sultan Kayqubad I (1220-1237) on the shore of Lake Beyşehir, its Great Palace measuring 50x35m; excavated from the 1960s, it yielded a renowned collection of polychrome figural ceramic tiles now in Konya's Karatay Museum.
vici:vici-69282.wikidataDescription: former palace in Beyşehir, Konya, Turkey

vici:vici-69838.label: Roman macellum (market place)
vici:vici-69838.description: Nero's Macellum Magnum, dedicated 59 CE on the Caelian Hill, was Rome's grand vaulted food market with marble counters and separate halls for butchers, fishmongers and produce sellers; its site likely underlies the church of S. Stefano Rotondo.
vici:vici-69838.wikidataDescription: a market building located on the Caelian Hill in Rome

vici:vici-69910.label: Agora
vici:vici-69910.description: Site of the agora of Greek Neapolis, founded c. 470 BCE, later the Roman forum; it lay beneath today's Piazza San Gaetano, with a Roman-era macellum and shops excavated beneath the Basilica of San Lorenzo Maggiore since the 1990s.

vici:vici-69982.label: Qasr Ain Es-Sil
vici:vici-69982.description: Small Umayyad-period farmhouse-palace with an attached bathhouse and two olive presses, 1.75km northeast of Azraq castle; built of basalt directly on bedrock, with Roman and Byzantine pottery attesting earlier occupation of the site.

vici:vici-69983.label: Qasr Al-Muwaqqar
vici:vici-69983.description: Umayyad desert palace built in 723 CE under Caliph Yazid II, 24 km southeast of Amman; little survives beyond carved acanthus capitals and a Kufic-inscribed water-depth gauge for its large cistern reservoir.

vici:vici-69984.label: Qasr Al-Qastal
vici:vici-69984.description: Among the oldest and most complete Umayyad desert castles, built c. 685-715 under Abd al-Malik or Yazid II; the complex's minaret is the only surviving Umayyad-era minaret, one of the oldest in the world.

vici:vici-69985.label: Qasr Hammam
vici:vici-69985.description: Umayyad bathhouse built under Caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik in the early 8th century, linked to nearby Qasr al-Hallabat 2 km west; its plan closely resembles the frescoed bath at Qusayr Amra.

vici:vici-69986.label: Qasr Mshash
vici:vici-69986.description: Sprawling 8th-century Umayyad way-station on Wadi Mshash covering roughly 2 sq km, with a caravanserai-like building, bathhouse, reservoirs and cisterns serving traffic between Amman and Wadi Sirhan; excavated by the German Archaeological Institute since 2011.

vici:vici-69988.label: Qasr Tuba
vici:vici-69988.description: Unfinished 8th-century Umayyad palace built c. 743 CE by order of Caliph al-Walid II for his sons, the southernmost of Jordan's desert castles, noted for its deep wells and early brick-vaulted construction.

vici:vici-69990.label: Umm Al-Walid
vici:vici-69990.description: Umayyad settlement (early 8th century) southeast of Madaba with two contemporary qasrs, a mosque, and remains from Bronze Age through Roman occupation; uniquely for the region, an Umayyad settlement built directly amid a Christian community.

vici:vici-70125.label: Smitthus, Forum
vici:vici-70125.description: Forum of Simitthus (Chemtou), Tunisia's source of prized golden Numidian marble; built over Numidian royal tombs and a native temple, only the basilica's massive apse survives. Excavated since the late 1960s by a Tunisian-German team led by Friedrich Rakob.

vici:vici-71498.label: Lavello
vici:vici-71498.description: Site of ancient Forentum, a Daunian-Samnite settlement absorbed by Rome in 318/315 BC; excavations on the Gravetta hill have revealed a 3rd-century BC sanctuary and traces of an associated town.

vici:vici-72087.label: Tall el-Hammam
vici:vici-72087.description: Fortified Middle Bronze Age city in the Jordan Valley with a monumental palace complex on the upper tell; excavated since 2005 by Trinity Southwest University, and proposed by some archaeologists as the site of biblical Sodom.

vici:vici-73102.label: Shadiyakh palace
vici:vici-73102.description: Palace and garden quarter of Nishapur founded by Tahirid governor Abdullah ibn Tahir al-Khurasani in the early 9th century; grew into an administrative and military settlement, later home to poet Attar of Nishapur, ruined by the 13th century.

vici:vici-76437.label: Forum
vici:vici-76437.description: Forum of Roman Tolosa (Toulouse), excavated in 1992-93 beneath Place Esquirol; its 27 x 35 m podium temple, probably the Capitolium of Jupiter, Juno and Minerva, was built in the later 1st century CE and destroyed around 400 CE.

vici:vici-77277.label: Fussboden des Forums
vici:vici-77277.description: Pavement of the forum of Roman Mediolanum (Milan), a 55 x 160 m plaza built under Augustus at the crossing of the cardo and decumanus; paving slabs and drainage remains were found beneath the Ambrosiana library and the crypt of San Sepolcro.

vici:vici-7910.label: Cryptoporticus of Reims
vici:vici-7910.description: A U-shaped underground horreum built c. 100 AD to support the forum of Roman Durocortorum (Reims); rediscovered in 1838, only its eastern gallery survives, one of just four such cryptoporticus galleries known in France.

vici:vici-81435.label: Lashkar-i Bazar (BALL 685) - Central palace
vici:vici-81435.description: One of three fortified palaces at Lashkari Bazar, the Ghaznavid rulers' winter residence near Bost; the Central Palace (32x52m) may predate the adjoining Ghaznavid North and South Palaces, possibly dating to the Samanid period.

vici:vici-81602.label: Mundigak - Palace
vici:vici-81602.description: Bronze Age palace atop Tepe A at Mundigak, excavated by Jean-Marie Casal for DAFA (1951-58); its Period IV-V facade of engaged semi-columns marked the settlement's growth into a fortified city with palace and temple.

vici:vici-83640.label: Byzantine Forum
vici:vici-83640.description: A circular paved forum about 40 m across, built under Emperor Anastasius I in the late 6th century at Dyrrhachium (Durrës), echoing Constantinople's Forum of Constantine; long misidentified as a macellum before excavation clarified its civic function.

vici:vici-84416.label: Sang-e Siāh
vici:vici-84416.description: Achaemenid-period palace (site BH48) near Borazjan, excavated by Esmail Yaghmaei from the 1970s; the structure has since been entirely bulldozed and survives only in excavation records and publications.

vici:vici-84419.label: Bardak Siāh
vici:vici-84419.description: Achaemenid palace near Borazjan with a colonnaded hall comparable in plan to Pasargadae; unearthed in 1977 by Esmail Yaghmaei, with a 2005 dig yielding a relief of Darius I and gold sheets buried beside a column base.
vici:vici-84419.wikidataDescription: palace in Dashtestan County, Iranian national heritage site

vici:vici-8497.label: Puteoli, Macellum
vici:vici-8497.description: Flavian-era macellum (market hall) of Roman Puteoli, excavated 1750-53; discovery of a Serapis statue there caused it to be misidentified as a Temple of Serapis until Charles Dubois recognized its commercial function in 1907.
vici:vici-8497.wikidataDescription: market building of the Roman colony of Puteoli, now the city of Pozzuoli in southern Italy

vici:vici-8510.label: Orange Remains of Roman Forum
vici:vici-8510.description: Excavated remains of the forum of Roman Arausio (Orange), founded 35 BC for veterans of Legio II Augusta; 1920s digs revealed a basilica, temple, and curia beneath the modern town center.

vici:vici-86800.label: Forum of Sentinum
vici:vici-86800.description: Forum and urban baths of Sentinum, the Umbrian town near which Rome's legions under Fabius Rullianus and Decius Mus crushed a Samnite-Gallic-Etruscan-Umbrian coalition at the decisive Battle of Sentinum in 295 BC.

vici:vici-89755.label: Palace of Masud III
vici:vici-89755.description: Ghaznavid royal palace at Ghazni built for Sultan Mas'ud III (r. 1099-1115); excavated 1957-66, its courtyard bore a marble dado of roughly 510 carved panels with Persian verses praising Mahmud of Ghazna.

vici:vici-9993.label: Karales, Forum Romanum
vici:vici-9993.description: Forum of Roman Karales (Cagliari), sited beneath today's Piazza del Carmine; surviving inscriptions attest surrounding temples, granaries, the praetorium, a courthouse, and at least three bath complexes.

dare-21461.label: Theater at Letoon
dare-21461.description: Hellenistic theater at the sanctuary of Leto (Letoon), built around 100 BCE with a rock-cut cavea of 37 rows in two tiers; part of the UNESCO Xanthos-Letoon site.

building:281201084.label: New Palace at Assur
building:281201084.description: Middle Assyrian king Tukulti-Ninurta I (r. 1233-1197 BC) built this ~27,000 sq m royal residence at Assur, known by its Sumerian name Elugalumunkurkurra ('House of the King, Lord of the Lands'); it fell into ruin after his reign, unmaintained once he founded his new capital Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta.

dare-37236.label: Bertelles
dare-37236.description: A fortified rural basilica in Cyrenaica, probably dating to the 6th century CE, associated with nearby farmsteads and tombs of Roman-period date; part of the Romano-Byzantine limes system of fortified rural sites (qsur).

dare-37237.label: Basilica near Ras el-Hilal
dare-37237.description: A 6th-century Byzantine church near Ras el-Hilal (ancient Naustathmus) in Cyrenaica, with its altar at the west end, a baptistery in the southwest corner, and relics of St Andrew; used until the Arab conquest of Cyrenaica in 643 CE.

dare-43726.label: Church of Mren
dare-43726.description: Armenian domed cathedral built c. 631-639 under Prince Nerses Kamsarakan and Bishop Theophilus, bearing reliefs commemorating Emperor Heraclius's return of the True Cross to Jerusalem; the largest surviving 7th-century Armenian domed basilica.
dare-43726.wikidataDescription: Armenian church built in the 7th century in Digor, Kars, Turkey

dare-21102.label: Apa Bane, Mon.
dare-21102.description: Coptic monastery in the Minya Governorate associated with the burial of the 4th-century hermit Saint Fana (Apa Bane); his tomb was identified by an Austrian-led archaeological team in 1992, and the present monastic structure is traditionally dated to the 12th century.

building:757392272.label: Crown Prince's Palace at Assur
building:757392272.description: Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib built this residence near Assur's southeastern city wall by the Tigris for his son Ashur-ili-muballissu; its existence is documented through numerous inscribed stone foundation blocks recording the construction.

dare-42178.label: Santa Maria in Portuno
dare-42178.description: A Roman-period vicus and villa near a Cesano River ford linking the Via Flaminia to the coast, with an excavated industrial quarter for brick and ceramic production; a monastery here is first recorded in 1090.

vici:vici-17599.label: Foro Grumentum
vici:vici-17599.description: Forum of the Roman municipium of Grumentum in Lucania (Basilicata). University of Verona excavations (2005-2014) uncovered three temples, the basilica, comitium and curia, plus the full forum porticus and piazza.

vici:vici-17755.label: Roman Forum, Athens
vici:vici-17755.description: Roman Agora of Athens, built 27-17 BC (possibly 10 BC) by architect Eucles of Marathon with funds from Augustus, fulfilling a pledge Julius Caesar made in 51 BC; entered through the Gate of Athena Archegetis.

vici:vici-17786.label: Agora, Messene
vici:vici-17786.description: Agora of ancient Messene, founded in the 3rd century BC, covering roughly 4 hectares and enclosed by four stoas; housed the Bouleuterion, Prytaneion, and a central shrine to the mythical queen Messene.

vici:vici-17808.label: Forum Thessalonica
vici:vici-17808.description: Roman Forum of Thessaloniki, built in the late 2nd century AD over the earlier Hellenistic agora, covering ca. 2 hectares with two-storey Corinthian colonnades and an odeion; excavated from 1966.
vici:vici-17808.wikidataDescription: historic Roman plaza in Thessaloniki, Greece

vici:vici-17896.label: Palace, Gerra
vici:vici-17896.description: Part of Gerrha, a fortified Hellenistic-period settlement (c. 330-30 BC) of the Ituraean Arabs in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, near modern Aanjar; no specific history of the palace building itself is attested beyond this.

vici:vici-23671.label: Stadtmauer
vici:vici-23671.description: Known as the Naumachia of Taormina, this Roman brick retaining wall (122m long, 5m high, with 18 large niches) was built in the 2nd century AD to buttress the hillside and enclose a water cistern; despite the name given in 1764, it never staged naval battles.

vici:vici-29293.label: Ebla, Southern Vizier Palace
vici:vici-29293.description: Built at the foot of the south side of Ebla's acropolis during the city's 'Third Kingdom' period (c. 2300 BC); served as the residence of Ebla's Grand Vizier, the highest official after the king.

vici:vici-30925.label: Royal Palace
vici:vici-30925.description: Citadel and royal residence of an unnamed Thracian king at an ancient Thracian city near Karlovo, Bulgaria, founded late 6th-early 5th century BC; discovered in 1993 and excavated since 2005 by archaeologist Kostadin Kisyov.

vici:vici-34198.label: Palace
vici:vici-34198.description: A palace building at Tell Chuera (ancient Harbe) in northern Syria, a site inhabited from the 4th millennium BC that grew into a major city during the 3rd-millennium Early Dynastic period.

vici:vici-71936.label: Forum
vici:vici-71936.description: A Roman-era forum/commercial building on the Hunnerberg at Nijmegen (ancient Ulpia Noviomagus Batavorum), dated to around 240 CE; its courtyard-building foundations, uncovered during urban development, are still marked out in the modern street pavement.

vici:vici-83372.label: Sasamon
vici:vici-83372.description: Roman theater at Segisamo (modern Sasamón), a Turmogi settlement where Augustus based a military camp in 26 BC during the Cantabrian Wars; only the scaena and part of an aqueduct conduit survive on a hill south of the town.

vici:vici-84197.label: Maruvium Theater
vici:vici-84197.description: Theater at Marruvium, capital of the Marsi on Lake Fucino, built during the city's 1st-century-AD monumentalization alongside an amphitheater, gymnasium, and baths; Strabo and Pliny called the town splendidissima civitas.

vici:vici-84199.label: Abella theater
vici:vici-84199.description: The surviving Roman entertainment structure at ancient Abella (Avella) is an amphitheater, not a theater: built in reticulate masonry in the 1st century BC against the city walls, comparable in size to Pompeii's amphitheater.

vici:vici-84204.label: Cosilianum theater
vici:vici-84204.description: At Cosilinum (Padula), a Lucanian settlement that became a Roman municipium in 89 BC, a theater stood among public and sacred buildings at the foot of the hilltop town, alongside a temple and suburban villas.

dare-37385.label: S. Autonomos, Mon.
dare-37385.description: Monastery named for the bishop-martyr Autonomus, who fled Diocletian's persecution from Italy to Bithynia, founded a church there, and was killed by pagans during a festival c. 313 AD.

dare-18164.label: Amphithéâtre Gallo-Romain
dare-18164.description: Ruins of a large Gallo-Roman entertainment building (described variously as an amphitheater or theater) at the hamlet of Bout Levé, first identified in the early 19th century and excavated in 1870 by Abbé Jean-Benoît Cochet; it measures roughly 70-79 by 46 m.

dare-37243.label: S. Zion, Mon./Pharroa
dare-37243.description: Monastery of Holy Sion in the Lycian hinterland near ancient Pharroa, headed in the 6th century by its abbot Nicholas of Sion, a monk and healer later ordained bishop of Pinara.

dare-37361.label: S. Thekla, Mon.
dare-37361.description: The Great Basilica of Saint Thecla at Meryemlik near Seleucia (Silifke), built by Emperor Zeno in the later 5th century over her cave shrine as an early fusion of basilica and domed-church design; it became a major Byzantine pilgrimage centre.
dare-37361.wikidataDescription: rock church in Silifke, Mersin Province, Turkey

dare-22838.label: Theater of the Muses
dare-22838.description: Cut into the slope of Mount Helicon within the Valley of the Muses sanctuary near Thespiae, built in the late 3rd or early 2nd century BC to host the quadrennial Mouseia festival honoring the nine Muses with poetry, music, and drama contests.

dare-37363.label: Alexandros, Mon.
dare-37363.description: Syriac monastery on the Euphrates near Halawa (Syria), founded in 782 CE and dedicated to Alexander the Acoemete, 5th-century founder of the 'Sleepless Monks' (Acoemetae) order.

dare-37354.label: Symeon, Mon.
dare-37354.description: Monastery of Saint Simeon Stylites the Younger on the 'Wondrous Mountain' near Antioch (modern Samandağ, Hatay), founded 551 CE at the site of his third pillar; a major pilgrimage complex until sacked in 1084.

dare-37254.label: Hyrkania/Kastellion
dare-37254.description: A Hasmonean fortress built by John Hyrcanus or Alexander Jannaeus, later expanded by Herod the Great as a prison for political enemies; refounded in 492 AD as the Byzantine monastery of Kastellion by Sabbas the Sanctified.

dare-22925.label: Basilica di Sant'Agnese fuori le mura
dare-22925.description: Pope Honorius I built this basilica in the 7th century over the tomb of St. Agnes, replacing the earlier Constantinian rotunda; noted for its gilded 7th-century apse mosaic and upper-level matroneum galleries.

dare-21145.label: Nebo Mons (church)
dare-21145.description: Basilica first built in the second half of the 4th century atop Mount Nebo to commemorate the death of Moses, enlarged in the late 5th century and rebuilt in 597; its floor mosaics date to about 530.

dare-37075.label: Iohannes Urtius, Mon.
dare-37075.description: Monastery in the Tur Abdin region of southeastern Turkey whose history is recorded in John of Ephesus's 6th-century Lives of the Eastern Saints, one of the region's early Syriac Orthodox monastic communities.

dare-16983.label: Craon
dare-16983.description: Part of a Gallo-Roman sanctuary complex near Montbouy on the Loing river, the Chenevière amphitheater-theater hybrid and its adjoining baths developed during the 1st-2nd centuries AD and were listed a historic monument in 1862.

vici:vici-11758.label: Theatre Peramon Sud
