vici:vici-11758.description: Coordinates match the great Hellenistic theater on Pergamon's acropolis: built under the Attalid kings (3rd-2nd century BC) on a roughly 70-degree slope, the steepest of any ancient theater, with later Roman modifications and seating for about 10,000.

vici:vici-12000.label: Theatre Cyzicus
vici:vici-12000.description: The theater of Cyzicus, which Pliny the Elder claimed could hold 40,000 spectators (the largest reported in antiquity), though modern scholars consider this figure exaggerated and estimate a capacity closer to 10,000.

vici:vici-17455.label: Giugliano Theatre,I - LILIANUM
vici:vici-17455.description: A small covered theatre (odeon) built north of the Capitolium in the forum of Liternum, a Roman colony founded in 194 BC; excavated by Amedeo Maiuri in the 1930s, revealing its cavea, vomitoria and orchestra.

vici:vici-17923.label: Forum Ostia
vici:vici-17923.description: Ostia's civic center at the crossing of the Decumanus and Cardo Maximus, flanked by the Capitolium (built under Hadrian, c. 120 AD, dedicated to the Capitoline Triad) and the Temple of Roma and Augustus added under Tiberius.

vici:vici-17949.label: Forum of Trajan
vici:vici-17949.description: Rome's last and largest Imperial Forum, built by architect Apollodorus of Damascus with spoils from the Dacian Wars and dedicated in 112 AD; included the Basilica Ulpia and Trajan's Column.

vici:vici-18033.label: Macellum, Leptis Magna
vici:vici-18033.description: Marketplace built in 8 BC, funded by Punic magnate Annobal Tapapius Rufus per a bilingual Latin/Neo-Punic inscription; a porticoed courtyard uniquely including two octagonal tholoi among its shops.

vici:vici-18041.label: Severan Forum, Leptis Magna
vici:vici-18041.description: Monumental forum (c. 170 x 80 m) begun under Septimius Severus and completed by Caracalla in 216 AD, centered on a Corinthian octastyle temple to the Severan dynasty with colonnades of imported cipollino and Pentelic marble.

vici:vici-18046.label: Byzantine theatre, Ptolemais
vici:vici-18046.description: The smallest of Ptolemais's three theatres, converted into a roofed odeon and, in the 4th-5th century AD Byzantine period, further adapted to stage water spectacles (naumachiae).

vici:vici-18047.label: Greek theatre, Ptolemais
vici:vici-18047.description: One of three theatres in the Hellenistic-Roman city of Ptolemais, Cyrenaica; the smallest was later converted into an odeon adapted for staged water spectacles in the 4th-5th century AD.

vici:vici-22129.label: Roman forum
vici:vici-22129.description: Site of Aquae Balissae, a Roman spa town of the Pannonian Iasi people at modern Daruvar; its thermal complex, temple, forum and amphitheatre were visited by emperors Marcus Aurelius, Commodus, Septimius Severus and Constantine I.

vici:vici-22226.label: Roman theatre
vici:vici-22226.description: Theatre of the Greek colony of Issa on the island of Vis, built in the 1st-2nd century AD and later incorporated into the foundations of a Franciscan monastery; one of only four archaeologically confirmed Roman theatres in Croatia.

vici:vici-24655.label: Balsa
vici:vici-24655.description: Theatre of Balsa, a Roman port town of Lusitania on the Ria Formosa near modern Luz de Tavira, identified through geophysical survey alongside a hippodrome and harbour works; no remains are visible above ground.

vici:vici-24657.label: Balsa
vici:vici-24657.description: Theatre of Balsa, a Roman port town of Lusitania on the Ria Formosa near modern Luz de Tavira, identified through geophysical survey alongside a hippodrome and harbour works; no remains are visible above ground.

vici:vici-24772.label: Gortyn
vici:vici-24772.description: One of Gortyn's two Roman theatrical buildings: the Odeon, built mid-1st century BC, destroyed by the earthquake of 46/66 AD and rebuilt under Trajan around 100 AD, later reused to display the inscribed blocks of the Gortyn Law Code.

vici:vici-24773.label: Gortyn
vici:vici-24773.description: One of Gortyn's two Roman theatrical buildings: a new theatre erected on the city's eastern side during the Antonine-Severan period, comparable in size to the earlier Greek theatre at the foot of the acropolis.

vici:vici-24857.label: Alexandria Troas
vici:vici-24857.description: Large theatre of Alexandria Troas, built into a hillside with an estimated capacity of 10,000-12,000, dating to the Hellenistic period and modified under Roman rule, notably during Hadrian's reign.

vici:vici-24864.label: Alexandria Troas
vici:vici-24864.description: Large theatre of Alexandria Troas, built into a hillside with an estimated capacity of 10,000-12,000, dating to the Hellenistic period and modified under Roman rule, notably during Hadrian's reign.

vici:vici-25043.label: Stadion of Labraunda
vici:vici-25043.description: Stadium above the Sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos, built during the Hecatomnid dynasty's 4th-century BC monumentalization of the site under Mausolus and Idrieus; used for athletic contests during the sanctuary's Carian festivals.

vici:vici-25116.label: Masada
vici:vici-25116.description: Data flag: these coordinates match Herodium, not Masada (which is ~40km southeast) — likely a mislabel in the source. Herod the Great built this small theatre c.15 BC; Ehud Netzer uncovered its frescoed royal box in 2008, shortly before his death.

vici:vici-25850.label: Amastris - Sesamus
vici:vici-25850.description: Roman-period theatre at Amastris (Amasra), estimated to have seated about 5,000; the city was formed c.300 BC when the Achaemenid princess Amastris, niece of Darius III, merged four Ionian towns including Sesamus.

vici:vici-25909.label: Myndus [Myndos]
vici:vici-25909.description: Ruins of a theatre and stadium at Myndos, a Carian city refounded and repopulated by Hecatomnid satrap Mausolus in the mid-4th century BC; it withstood Alexander the Great's siege in 334 BC. Since eroded or built over.

vici:vici-25917.label: Myndus [Myndos]
vici:vici-25917.description: Ruins of a theatre and stadium at Myndos, a Carian city refounded and repopulated by Hecatomnid satrap Mausolus in the mid-4th century BC; it withstood Alexander the Great's siege in 334 BC. Since eroded or built over.

vici:vici-26146.label: Tralles, Stadium
vici:vici-26146.description: Stadium at Tralles, a major Carian city that surrendered peacefully to Alexander the Great in 334 BC and was rebuilt with Augustus's funding after a devastating 26 BC earthquake; birthplace of Hagia Sophia's architect Anthemius.

vici:vici-26181.label: Amantia, Theatre
vici:vici-26181.description: Hellenistic theatre at Amantia, capital of the Illyrian Amantes, built near the city's well-preserved 3rd-century BC stadium and a sanctuary of Aphrodite.

vici:vici-29261.label: Seleucia Pamphylian - Lybre, Council House?
vici:vici-29261.description: Semicircular building attached to the agora of ancient Lyrbe-Seleukeia in Pamphylia, tentatively identified as a bouleuterion (council house); the site's agora is considered the best-preserved example in the region, dated broadly to the Roman period.

vici:vici-31299.label: Lanciano Theatre - Anxanum
vici:vici-31299.description: Theatre of Anxanum (Lanciano), capital of the Frentani; its remains lie beneath the city's Archbishop's Palace alongside a Roman bath complex, built after Anxanum gained municipium status following the Social War (91-88 BCE).

vici:vici-31308.label: Tivoli Villa Adriana Amphitheatre
vici:vici-31308.description: Elliptical structure at the foot of the Piazza d'Oro in Hadrian's Villa (built 118-138 CE), long taken for a fish-pond or basin; 2024 excavations found it was built over an unrecorded, richly decorated Hadrianic complex demolished to make way for it.

vici:vici-31512.label: Ephesus, Tribune
vici:vici-31512.description: The Odeon (Bouleuterion) of Ephesus: a small semicircular theatre-cum-council-house built c.150 CE, endowed by Publius Vedius Antoninus and his wife Flavia Papiana, seating roughly 1,400-1,500 for both civic assembly and musical performance.

vici:vici-31534.label: Theater
vici:vici-31534.description: Antioch's Greek theatre, cut into the flank of Mount Silpius, was reportedly begun under Julius Caesar, enlarged by Agrippa and Tiberius, and finished under Trajan; its cavea substructures survived built into the mountainside.

vici:vici-33545.label: Theater
vici:vici-33545.description: The ancient theatre on the Munichia hill (modern Kastella) above Piraeus's Mounichia harbour, used for festivals and deme assembly meetings; the Athenian democratic assembly met here during the political crises of 411 and 404 BCE.

vici:vici-34312.label: Dura Europos Theatre
vici:vici-34312.description: A Roman amphitheatre built in 216 CE in the military quarter of Dura-Europos on the Euphrates, for the entertainment of the Roman garrison stationed there after Rome captured the city from Parthia in 165 CE.

vici:vici-34436.label: Ouasada theater
vici:vici-34436.description: A Roman-period theatre attested at Vasada (ancient Ouasada), a city of Lycaonia and later Isauria near modern Bostandere, Konya Province, Turkey; its bishops appear at early Byzantine church councils, but the theatre itself is little published.

vici:vici-36038.label: Felix Romuliana, Palace II?
vici:vici-36038.description: A fortified palace and memorial complex built from 298 AD by Emperor Galerius near his birthplace, named Felix Romuliana after his mother Romula; it contains at least two palace buildings, temples, and Galerius's planned mausoleum. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007.

vici:vici-4312.label: Amphitheatre Bulla Regia
vici:vici-4312.description: A small Roman amphitheatre at Bulla Regia in Tunisia, criticized in a sermon of Augustine of Hippo for its spectacles; it lay buried and was excavated only in 1960–61.

vici:vici-44943.label: Megalopolis, Bouleuterion
vici:vici-44943.description: The Thersilion, federal assembly hall of the Arcadian League at Megalopolis, built c.370–345 BC as a hypostyle hall with dozens of radiating columns seating up to roughly 8,700; destroyed by Cleomenes III of Sparta and never rebuilt.

vici:vici-49119.label: Ampfitheater
vici:vici-49119.description: The Roman theatre of Saguntum, built into the hillside below the city's castle in the mid-1st century AD; its semicircular cavea seated up to about 8,000 spectators. Declared a Bien de Interes Cultural in 1896, it still hosts performances today.

vici:vici-50315.label: Roman Theater
vici:vici-50315.description: Roman theatre of Parthicopolis near modern Sandanski, Bulgaria, built in the late 1st–early 2nd century AD at a cost of about 2.5 million sestertii; seated 5,800–6,000 and was later adapted for gladiatorial games before falling out of use as Christianity spread in the 4th century.

vici:vici-50607.label: Roman Theater
vici:vici-50607.description: A Roman theatre atop the Cerro de San Juan del Viso, seat of the earlier hilltop city of Complutum, is roughly 40 m in diameter and, per 2022 archaeological reports, the first Roman theatre documented in the Community of Madrid; it remains unexcavated because the land is privately held.

vici:vici-51051.label: Carteia Ampfitheater
vici:vici-51051.description: Carteia, granted colony status in 171 BC as the first Roman colony outside Italy, had an amphitheatre whose remains 19th-century antiquarians recorded as still traceable, though its construction date and capacity were never documented.

vici:vici-54793.label: Florentia Circus
vici:vici-54793.description: A hippodrome for Roman Florentia is inferred from the curved street plan at Croce del Trebbio near Piazza Santa Maria Novella, estimated at 200-220 m long and able to hold about 20,000 spectators; no physical remains have ever been excavated, and the earliest written reference dates only to 1375.

vici:vici-54811.label: Bosra, Palace of Sergius
vici:vici-54811.description: A late antique episcopal palace at Bosra (Roman Bostra), built in the 6th century as the residence of the Archbishop of the province of Arabia, adjacent to the cathedral of Saints Sergius, Bacchus and Leontius.

vici:vici-55312.label: Pompeiopolis in Paphlagonia, Odeon I
vici:vici-55312.description: The Odeon adjoins the Roman theatre of Pompeiopolis, capital of Paphlagonia founded by Pompey the Great around 64 BC; 2024 excavations found its seating rows reduced to lime beneath a 2-meter ash layer, alongside two fragmentary Aphrodite statues.

vici:vici-55313.label: Pompeiopolis in Paphlagonia, Odeon II
vici:vici-55313.description: Odeon adjoining the Roman theater at Pompeiopolis, capital of Roman Paphlagonia founded after Pompey's 64 BC reorganization of Pontus; excavation found its seating rows disintegrated to lime beneath a thick ash layer.

vici:vici-58395.label: Roman Ampfiteater
vici:vici-58395.description: Elliptical Roman amphitheater of ancient Asculum (Ascoli Piceno), probably built under Augustus; roughly 148 by 125 meters with a 450-meter circumference. Buried beneath modern Piazza San Tommaso, it was briefly exposed by excavation in 1974 then reburied.

vici:vici-59561.label: Roman Theater
vici:vici-59561.description: Roofed theater (theatrum tectum) of Interamna Lirenas near the forum, redeveloped in the later 1st century BC; about 45 by 26 meters, seating roughly 1,500, faced with imported Mediterranean marbles. Excavated by Cambridge University archaeologists since 2013.

vici:vici-60101.label: Henchir Toungara Theather
vici:vici-60101.description: Also known as ancient Cincari (Municipium Cincaritanum), a small Roman town near Tebourba in northern Tunisia best known for this structure; its remains are so scanty that scholars still dispute whether it was a theatre or an amphitheatre.

vici:vici-61519.label: Market
vici:vici-61519.description: Part of Gigthis, a Romanized Punic port on Tunisia's Gulf of Gabès; its forum (60.6 x 38.5 m), ringed by shops and official buildings, stood on a hill beside the Temple of Isis and Serapis.

vici:vici-62489.label: Amphitheater
vici:vici-62489.description: Part of the Roman spa settlement of Ad Mediam (modern Băile Herculane) in Dacia, built around thermal springs sacred to Hercules alongside baths, temples, and monuments serving the garrison and visitors from the 2nd century AD.

vici:vici-62738.label: Theatre
vici:vici-62738.description: The Roman theatre at Thugga (Dougga), funded and built by P. Marcius Quadratus in 168-169 AD, seated over 3,500 spectators and is among the best-preserved Roman theatres in North Africa.

vici:vici-62873.label: Roman Theater
vici:vici-62873.description: A small Roman theatre-like structure (possibly an odeon/bouleuterion) discovered beneath Wilson's Arch at Jerusalem's Western Wall, built c. 2nd century CE under Hadrian and left unfinished, likely due to the Bar Kokhba Revolt (132-135 CE) or Hadrian's death; seated roughly 200 people.

vici:vici-63224.label: Théâtre gallo-romain du Mortier Noir
vici:vici-63224.description: Gallo-Roman theatre built on the site of Silva Martis (modern Petit-Mars, Loire-Atlantique) in the 1st century CE, part of a rural sanctuary complex on the road from Angers to Vannes; its facade wall spanned just over 73 m with a 57 m cavea, excavated in the 1880s.

vici:vici-63633.label: Roman Theater
vici:vici-63633.description: Roman theatre of Patavium (Padua), built in the Augustan era beneath what is now Prato della Valle; the city's second-largest ancient structure after its amphitheater, progressively stripped of stone for medieval Padua and Venice (including Venice's Rialto Bridge) before being re-excavated in 2017.

vici:vici-66611.label: Roman Theater
vici:vici-66611.description: The Gallo-Roman theatre of Noviomagus Lexoviorum (Lisieux), at Saint-Désir, was built in the 2nd century AD with a cavea about 109 m in diameter; it was later reworked and classified a French historic monument in 1984.

vici:vici-69987.label: Qasr Shabeeb
vici:vici-69987.description: A square fortified palace (qasr) near Zarqa, Jordan, built in the Roman period (c. 3rd century AD) and later restored and reused under the Umayyads, Mamluks, and Ottomans as a way-station on the Hajj pilgrimage route.

vici:vici-84238.label: CANETONUM THEATRE
vici:vici-84238.description: A Gallo-Roman theatre was excavated in 1861-1862 and 1986 near the pilgrimage sanctuary of Mercury Canetonensis at Berthouville, the findspot of the famous 2nd-century Berthouville silver treasure dedicated to the god.

vici:vici-84270.label: JULIA CONSTANTIA OSSET THEATER
vici:vici-84270.description: A Roman theater is attested at Iulia Constantia Osset (San Juan de Aznalfarache, near Seville) by the inscription CIL II 1255 recording games (ludi); no visible remains survive today.

dare-37387.label: Kosmas kai Damianos, Mon.
dare-37387.description: Monastery church of Saints Cosmas and Damian ("Kosmidion") on the Golden Horn near Blachernae, a major shrine of the healer-saints traditionally linked to Theodosius II's reign; rebuilt with mosaics and marble by Emperor Michael IV in the 11th century.

dare-37388.label: Metanoia Mon.
dare-37388.description: The Metanoia ("Repentance") convent founded by Empress Theodora, wife of Justinian I, in a former imperial palace on the Bosphorus as a refuge for roughly 500 former prostitutes freed by her anti-trafficking reforms.

dare-37321.label: Palaiomonastero
dare-37321.description: An Early Byzantine basilica (6th-7th century AD) on the northern coast of Samos, one of several early Christian basilicas built on the island in this period.

dare-37360.label: Sannabadae, Mon.
dare-37360.description: A Byzantine monastery (probably 6th century) built directly across a Neo-Hittite rock relief at Ambarderesi near Ivriz in Konya province, its placement deliberately continuing the older site's sacred tradition.

dare-37402.label: Barlaamus
dare-37402.description: Tradition holds that the 4th-century monk Barlaam destroyed a pagan temple on this site near Antioch; a small church was built here in the early 6th century, later rebuilt as a Georgian monastery (c.950-1050) and used until 1268.

dare-21103.label: Apa Apollo
dare-21103.description: The Coptic monastery of Apa Apollo at Bawit, founded c. 385/390 by Saint Apollo and housing about 500 monks at its peak; it grew into a major monastic complex of some 40 hectares before its abandonment around the 10th century.

dare-37299.label: Apa Psote, Mon./Amba Bisada
dare-37299.description: Dedicated to Bishop Psote (Bisada) of Ebsay, martyred by beheading at Antinoë in 300 CE during the Diocletianic Persecution for refusing to renounce his Christian faith.

dare-42931.label: Mushabbak Basilica
dare-42931.description: A well-preserved Byzantine three-aisled basilica near Aleppo, Syria, built in the third quarter of the 5th century (c. 470), likely as a pilgrim way-station on the route to the shrine of Saint Simeon Stylites.

dare-37066.label: Apostoli, Mon.
dare-37066.description: Arakelots ("Holy Apostles") Monastery near Mush in historic Taron, traditionally founded by Gregory the Illuminator to house apostolic relics but likely built in the 11th century under Tornikian rule; a major center of learning in the 12th–13th centuries, dynamited around 1960.

dare-10653.label: Plöckenpass
dare-10653.description: A Roman-era pass sanctuary at the summit of Plöckenpass (Monte Croce Carnico) in the Carnic Alps, where travelers on the road from Aquileia left votive dedications to Jupiter Optimus Maximus for safe passage; known chiefly from Latin inscriptions including the Hermia dedication, in use 1st century BC–3rd century AD.

dare-11691.label: Oberdorla
dare-11691.description: Germanic sacrificial bog sanctuary used from the Hallstatt period (6th century BCE) to the Migration Age (5th century CE), the largest known Iron Age cult site in Central Europe; 1957-64 excavations recovered wooden idols linked to Wodan, Freyr, and Diana.

dare-1211.label: Meckel
dare-1211.description: Extensive but only partly excavated Gallo-Roman temple complex on the Via Agrippa between Trier and Bitburg; building inscriptions and statues of Fortuna and Jupiter attest at least two temples, one dedicated to Mercury.

dare-1293.label: Tabernae
dare-1293.description: Gallo-Roman sanctuary on the Metzenberg above the roadside vicus of Tabernae (Tawern), built from the early 1st century CE and used until the late 4th; 1986-88 excavations found seven temple buildings in a walled precinct, chiefly dedicated to Mercury.

dare-13742.label: [Camelaria]
dare-13742.description: Ancient Camelaria, identified with the open-air Gallo-Roman spring sanctuary of Source des Roches at Chamalières; excavated 1968–71, it yielded roughly 3,500 carved wooden ex-votos and a Gaulish curse tablet, used mainly in the first half of the 1st century AD.

dare-1537.label: Elst
dare-1537.description: Grand Gallo-Roman temple (23 x 30 m, once c.17 m high) built c.100 CE over an earlier Batavian open-air shrine, dedicated to Hercules Magusanus, chief god of the Batavians; among the largest Roman temples north of the Alps.

dare-15763.label: Baron-sur-Odon
dare-15763.description: The Celto-Roman sanctuary of Le Mesnil at Baron-sur-Odon, near the civitas capital of the Viducasses (Vieux/Aregenua); excavated 1952–56, it revealed an indigenous cult site with a dodecagonal building and a mock 'symbolic' burial, predating its Gallo-Roman rebuilding.

dare-15766.label: Belbèze-en-Comminges
dare-15766.description: The Gallo-Roman sanctuary of Pédégas at Belbèze, discovered in 1964 and excavated by G. Manière 1965–67: a temple and spring-fed pool where numerous votive altars and small offering vessels were found, many deliberately broken; the cult site was abandoned/destroyed by the late 4th century.

dare-15778.label: Allègre-les-Fumades
dare-15778.description: A Gallo-Roman secondary settlement and water-cult site at Arlende/Fumades (1st century BC–3rd century AD), where a spring basin yielded a tiled pool, mosaics, coins, and about thirty votive altars dedicated to protective water nymphs; the cult ended after Theodosius's anti-pagan edicts.

dare-16592.label: Vibinum
dare-16592.description: Sanctuary atop ancient Vibinum (Bovino, Apulia), identified by dedicatory inscriptions to Mars and Bellona, comprising a rectangular and an oval temple; the site also held temples to Apollo and Hercules, the latter later replaced by a church.

dare-16974.label: Margerides
dare-16974.description: The Gallo-Roman sanctuary of Pièces-Grandes at Margerides: an enclosure containing three square fana, the main one c.12.8m per side with a 7m cella; occupation ran from a late 1st-century BC Gallic phase (coins of the Lemovices) through Roman use into the 4th century AD.

dare-16985.label: Le Mont-Dore
dare-16985.description: A Gallo-Roman thermal sanctuary at Le Mont-Dore, built over springs venerated since Gaulish times (excavated wooden basins predate Roman work); Roman baths and a temple, later called the "Panthéon," operated on the site into late antiquity.

dare-17219.label: Minerva Cabardiacensis
dare-17219.description: A healing sanctuary of Minerva Cabardiacensis, a Celtic-Ligurian goddess assimilated to Minerva Medica, stood near Travo in the Val Trebbia (Piacenza); attested only by inscriptions, including Trajan's Tabula Alimentaria of Veleia, and votive ex-votos recovered along the Trebbia.

dare-17243.label: Nemora Vacunae
dare-17243.description: Nemora Vacunae, sacred groves of the Sabine goddess Vacuna in the upper Velino valley near Rieti, are recorded by Pliny the Elder and fed the spring of Lacus Cutiliae; Horace mentions a decayed shrine to the goddess near his own Sabine farm.

dare-17304.label: Menthon-Saint-Bernard
dare-17304.description: Gallo-Roman thermal baths at Menthon-Saint-Bernard on Lake Annecy, roughly thirty rooms across some 900 m2 with a caldarium wing, in use from the 1st to 4th century AD; classified a monument historique in 1990.

dare-17398.label: Nanteuil-sur-Aisne
dare-17398.description: The Gallic and Gallo-Roman sanctuary of Le Népellier, about 1.5 km from Acy-Romance, was an oval ditched enclosure with a fanum revealed by aerial survey; excavation yielded Roman coins, broken weapons, and human bone, with cult use into the 4th century AD.

dare-17527.label: Octon
dare-17527.description: A Gallo-Roman water sanctuary (fanum) tied to a votive spring cult was identified at Octon; published by archaeologist Henri Prades with J. Lugagne, R. Majurel and J. Ménager as "Un sanctuaire des Eaux à Octon (Hérault)" (Tradition celtique, 1969).

dare-17551.label: Saint-Laurent-les-Bains
dare-17551.description: A hot spring (53°C, among the hottest in France) known in antiquity as "Sanctus Laurentius Balneis" was used for its therapeutic waters in Roman times, served by a nearby Roman road, giving the site its name.

dare-17593.label: Saint-Andéol
dare-17593.description: An 11x8m Gallo-Roman fanum was excavated in 1956 beside a menhir and stone circle on the shore of Lac de Saint-Andéol (Aubrac); votive deposits of pottery, human/animal figurines, and coins spanning Augustus to Constantius II attest a long Gaulish-to-Roman water cult.

dare-17638.label: Masamas
dare-17638.description: A Gallo-Roman sanctuary of twin temples within a walled precinct with an east-facing propylon, near Saint-Léomer (Vienne); it began as a Celtic-tradition temple c. 50 BC, was rebuilt in masonry c. 40-50 AD, and was abandoned in the 3rd century AD. Discovered in 1945 by Abbé Florentin Reix, classified a historic monument in 1973.

dare-17683.label: Saint-Alban-les-Eaux
dare-17683.description: Mineral springs frequented since Roman times; basin-cleaning in 1834 and 1859 recovered numerous coins and medals, many dated 70-160 AD, indicating a votive/therapeutic cult of the waters in antiquity.

dare-17690.label: Saint-Galmier
dare-17690.description: Site of the Gallo-Roman vicus Auditiacus; 1844 excavations uncovered Roman thermal baths dated from the mid-2nd to mid-4th century AD, and finds near the Aubigny locality (a Roman vase, imperial coins, and cremated human/animal remains) point to associated ritual activity.

dare-17703.label: Thaumiers
dare-17703.description: Aerial survey in 1982 revealed a Gallo-Roman religious complex at 'Le Moulin des Gaumins' — two temples and a theatre enclosed together — published as a sanctuary-with-theatre by J. Holmgren in 1983.

dare-17809.label: *Ganuenta?
dare-17809.description: Roman-era port sanctuary on the Scheldt at Colijnsplaat, dedicated to the seafarers' goddess Nehalennia; over 160 votive altars dredged from the estuary since 1970, given by merchants trading salt, wine, and pottery.

dare-18046.label: Pierre Écrite
dare-18046.description: Rock-cut Latin inscription (2nd quarter of the 5th century) commissioned by praetorian prefect Claudius Postumus Dardanus and his wife Naevia Galla, commemorating a road built through the gorge and the founding of the Christian settlement Théopolis.

dare-18049.label: Lachau
dare-18049.description: The 'Luminaïre' sanctuary near Lachau, a Gallo-Roman votive-deposit site reusing an old quarry, yielded large quantities of terracotta oil lamps and other votive offerings excavated in the 19th century; finds are held in the Gap museum.

dare-18076.label: Roquepertuse
dare-18076.description: Iron-Age Celto-Ligurian sanctuary (3rd century BC) near Velaux, famed for carved stone pillars with niches holding severed skulls of male warriors under 40, evidence of a head cult; destroyed by Rome in 124 BC, finds now in Marseille's Musée d'Archéologie Méditerranéenne.

dare-18100.label: Puy Lautard
dare-18100.description: A hilltop fanum (775m) at Saint-Pierre-Bellevue with two cellae, rebuilt in stone over an earlier shrine and occupied 1st-4th c. AD; excavated altars bear carved images of Apollo and Neptune. Classified monument historique in 1990.

dare-18113.label: Saint-Gervais
dare-18113.description: A round Gallo-Roman fanum with polygonal ambulatory, a temple form typical of western Gaul; the nearby villa 'Villa Bonna' gave rise to the later town, alongside other scattered Gallo-Roman remains in the commune.

dare-18123.label: Saint-Aubin-sur-Mer
dare-18123.description: At Cap Romain, Eugène Eblé's 1942-44 excavations found a 1st-century Gallic sanctuary and a Gallo-Roman villa with baths beneath a later Frankish cemetery; a carved Mother-Goddess statue was recovered there in 1943.

dare-18144.label: Gisacum
dare-18144.description: A vast hexagonal sanctuary-city (c.250ha) of the Aulerci Eburovici, centered on a monumental temple to Apollo and Jupiter with baths, theatre and forum; founded early 1st c. AD, it flourished 2nd-3rd c. before abrupt abandonment.

dare-18162.label: Les Jaillants
dare-18162.description: A fanum sanctuary at 824m on the Millevaches plateau (Col des Géants), Pradines; excavations 1959-1982 revealed pre-Roman Gallic-tradition pottery beneath two successive temples, occupied 1st-2nd c. AD and abandoned in the 3rd century.

dare-18233.label: Mont Sacon
dare-18233.description: Pyrenean summit sanctuary dedicated to Jupiter; 1956-57 excavations by Georges Fouet and Andrée Soutou recovered fragments and bases of white marble votive altars, now in the Musée Saint-Raymond, Toulouse.

dare-18240.label: La Capte
dare-18240.description: Rock-cut, wall-less sanctuary of Aristaeus on the Giens peninsula near Olbia, used continuously from the late 2nd century BC to the early 1st century AD; excavations (1973-1982) yielded over 40,000 pottery fragments.

dare-18500.label: Loubers
dare-18500.description: Gallo-Roman rural sanctuary (fanum du Camp-Ferrus), excavated 1968-1975 under abbé Marius Bessou; a quadrangular enclosure (~70x42m) held successive cult buildings from the late La Tène period into the late 3rd century AD, ending in a fire.

dare-19005.label: Sudelfels
dare-19005.description: The Quellheiligtum Sudelfels near Ihn (Wallerfangen): a Gallo-Roman spring sanctuary founded in the early 1st century AD, its octagonal temple honoring the healing goddess Sirona, with further shrines to Apollo, Minerva, Mercury and Rosmerta; excavated 1981-84.

dare-19320.label: Porcetum
dare-19320.description: Porcetum, a Roman vicus at Aachen-Burtscheid, held a nymphaeum sanctuary to the healing god Apollo Grannus; excavated in 1969, the shrine enclosed a sacred spring and fed an aqueduct to Aquae Granni, with a dedicatory altar dated 108-119 CE.

dare-19321.label: Nöthen
dare-19321.description: Multi-building Gallo-Roman temple complex (Tempelbezirk Pesch) on the Addig hill between Nöthen and Pesch, dedicated chiefly to the Matronae Vacallinehae; built 1st-4th century AD, excavated by Hans Lehner 1913-1918, comprising three temples and a 120m portico.

dare-19335.label: Bierbach
dare-19335.description: A Gallo-Roman temple precinct on the Rödersberg near Bierbach (Blieskastel), comprising two temples within a roughly 60-metre walled enclosure; excavated in 1927 by state conservator Carl Klein after pottery sherds turned up during forestry work.

dare-19475.label: Lenus Mars
dare-19475.description: The Trier sanctuary 'Am Irminenwingert' was the chief cult center of the Treveran healing god Lenus Mars: a walled precinct over 100m per side with a great temple, baths, shrines and a theater, used until Emperor Gratian's reign (d. 383).

dare-19898.label: Merkurtempel
dare-19898.description: Gallo-Roman temple to Mercury and his Gallic consort Rosmerta near Waldesch by Koblenz, discovered 1898 and excavated in the 1920s; a ~19x18m walled cella stood within a temenos ~106m across with a spring, on the site of an earlier Celtic sacred precinct.

dare-20086.label: Saint-Germain-le-Rocheux
dare-20086.description: Site of the Fanum du Tremblois, a square Gallo-Roman temple with cella and surrounding gallery built over an earlier Iron Age Celtic cult site in the Châtillonnais forest; yielded ex-votos of divinities, animals, and votive pillars, and was destroyed around 337 CE.

dare-20087.label: Essarois
dare-20087.description: Healing sanctuary of Apollo Vindonnus at a curative spring near Châtillon-sur-Seine, with a surviving pediment inscribed to the god and the spirit of the springs; wooden and stone ex-votos (hands, body parts, many eyes) suggest pilgrims sought cures for eye ailments.

dare-20114.label: Pas de la Selle
dare-20114.description: The "fortin-sanctuaire" (fortified cult building) of Pas de la Selle on the Causse du Larzac at La Panouse-de-Cernon, excavated 1960-63 by André Soutou; coins and terra sigillata from the La Graufesenque potteries date its main use to the 1st-2nd centuries CE.

dare-20156.label: Saint-Plancard
dare-20156.description: Gallo-Roman sanctuary dedicated to Mars-Sutugius, a local warrior god known almost solely from this site; some forty votive altars, stelae, funerary cippi, statues and architectural fragments were found reused in the walls of the later church built over the temple.

dare-20713.label: Bausendorf
dare-20713.description: A Gallo-Roman ambulatory temple (Umgangstempel) with a square 7m cella inside a 15m gallery, set within a c. 40x50m temenos, was partially excavated in 1941 and 1975 southwest of Bausendorf, alongside a small vicus.

dare-20715.label: Otrang
dare-20715.description: The Roman villa rustica complex at Otrang near Fließem (1st-4th c. AD), with its 60+ room manor house and baths, also included a dedicated temple precinct within the estate grounds.

dare-20716.label: Gusenburg
dare-20716.description: A Gallo-Roman ambulatory temple (Umgangstempel) stood at the boundary of Gusenburg with Hermeskeil; iron-stained red soil and Roman pottery/tile finds from the site are commemorated in the village's coat of arms.

dare-20719.label: Horperath
dare-20719.description: A small Gallo-Roman temple precinct dated to around 150 AD was excavated in 1936 by the Landesmuseum Bonn in the "An den Vier Bäumen" field near Horperath, after a farmer discovered building rubble and roof tiles there.

dare-20721.label: Elzerath
dare-20721.description: Near the Roman road to Belginum, a stone-walled sacred precinct (c. 83.5 x 35.5 m, called "Judenkirchhof") near Elzerath contained a small temple building (c. 4.5 x 4.7 m) excavated in 1963, dated to the late Roman period.

dare-20751.label: La Chapelle-Marcousse
dare-20751.description: A monumental Gallo-Roman rural fanum measuring 50m per side stood at La Chapelle-Marcousse, far exceeding the typical 10-17m size of Auvergne temples; only Landeyrat's sanctuary matches it in scale, per a 2006 regional inventory.

dare-20763.label: Temple de Mars
dare-20763.description: The largest known Gallo-Roman temple sanctuary in Brittany, an octagonal temple built in the late 1st century AD at Fanum Martis (Corseul), capital of the Coriosolites, dedicated to Mars syncretized with a native Celtic war god.

dare-20820.label: Mithraeum
dare-20820.description: A Mithraic temple on the Heiligenberg's eastern slope at Heidelberg-Neuenheim, discovered in 1838, yielding a tauroctony relief and statues of Cautes and Cautopates; finds of four more statues in 1953 suggest a second, later Mithraeum on the site.

dare-20835.label: Nattenheim
dare-20835.description: Gallo-Roman Umgangstempel (ambulatory temple) on the Nattenheimer Kopf beside the Via Agrippa, 6 km north of Bitburg; cella 6.67 x 6.15 m within an 11.85 x 10.25 m surround with Tuscan-order red-sandstone columns, excavated in 1875 by Ernst aus'm Weerth.

dare-20840.label: Niersbach
dare-20840.description: Site of a temple to the local Gallo-Roman god Jutarabus, attested by a Latin votive inscription (found 1619/1669 while plowing) recording its dedication by Quintus Solimarius; the altar stones, later built into Arenrath's church portal, were moved to the Trier museum in 1824.

dare-20842.label: Röhl
dare-20842.description: A small Gallo-Roman temple identified from an 1886 find of square stone foundations, roof tiles, pottery sherds, and Roman copper coins about 1.2 km north of Röhl, near a Roman settlement and an Iron Age burial field in the Eifel.

dare-20845.label: Wolsfeld
dare-20845.description: The Umgangstempel von Wolsfeld, a Gallo-Roman ambulatory temple on the Galgenhöhe ridge above the Nims valley, with a 4x4 m cella inside a 9x9 m colonnade, possibly linked to Lenus Mars; exposed by 1919/20 roadworks after 19th-century finds of glass urns and a statue head.

dare-20846.label: Schleidweiler-Rodt
dare-20846.description: A rural sanctuary northwest of Schleidweiler excavated in 1932-33, comprising three stone temples, the largest a 13.3 m square temple built in the early 4th century AD and a 5.55 m temple of the 2nd-3rd century; finds included coins from Augustus to the late 4th century and bronze dedication-inscription fragments.

dare-20848.label: Eisenach
dare-20848.description: A Roman sanctuary near Eisenach in the Eifel, attested archaeologically to roughly 80-300 AD, situated near a Late Iron Age cemetery used from about 450 BC to the turn of the era.

dare-20849.label: Graach
dare-20849.description: A Gallo-Roman sanctuary at Graach enclosed by a 56x53 m temenos wall around a 6x6.7 m cult building, in use from the late Iron Age into the early 5th century and likely dedicated to Minerva per a terracotta figurine inscribed MIN; excavations in 1933 and 1978 yielded mother-goddess figurines, coins, fibulae, and a three-figure terracotta group.

dare-20853.label: Landscheid
dare-20853.description: A Gallo-Roman Mercury sanctuary (Merkurheiligtum) stood at Landscheid/Burg beside a Celtic ringwall; a sandstone altar inscribed 'Deo Mercurio', found nearby in 1984, is linked to the site excavated by the Rhineland Landesmuseum Trier.

dare-20854.label: Mürlenbach
dare-20854.description: A Gallo-Roman temple to Caprio, an otherwise unattested local deity, was uncovered in 1840 at Hasselseifen near Mürlenbach; its limestone dedication tablet is held in the Rhineland State Museum in Trier.

dare-20872.label: Nideggen
dare-20872.description: The Heiligtum von Nideggen-Abenden was a Roman-era sanctuary in Nideggen's Abenden district dedicated to the Matronae Veteranehae; fragments of at least 54 votive stone altars from the 1st-2nd centuries AD were excavated there.

dare-20873.label: Pier
dare-20873.description: A Roman-era sanctuary at Inden-Pier attested by reused Matronae votive stones and a ground plan resembling the temple precinct at Bad Münstereifel-Pesch, likely dedicated to the Matronae Alusneihae; excavated by Bonn University from 2011 before the site was destroyed by lignite mining.

dare-21069.label: Surb Tadeos
dare-21069.description: Armenian tradition holds that the Apostle Thaddeus founded this church in 68 AD, making it one of Christianity's oldest; rebuilt in 1329 after earthquake damage, with 10th-century apse remains, and inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage in 2008 with two other Armenian sites in Iran.

dare-21071.label: Deir Abou Menas
dare-21071.description: Pilgrimage complex built around the tomb of the martyred Roman soldier Menas (d. 296 AD), expanded into a basilica, baptistery, and pilgrim town under Emperor Arcadius (395-408); a major early Christian healing shrine and UNESCO World Heritage site since 1979.

dare-21293.label: Danielsberg
dare-21293.description: Hilltop cult site above Kolbnitz in Carinthia's Möll valley; a Roman temple to Hercules replaced an earlier Celtic sanctuary, attested by an inscription recording its restoration by Caius Donnicius Rufinus and Valeria Attica, and was succeeded by an early Christian chapel around 313.

dare-21934.label: Akrokorinthos
dare-21934.description: Fortified acropolis of Corinth crowned by the 5th-century-BC Temple of Aphrodite, home to a cult statue of Armed Aphrodite; its sanctuaries were largely abandoned or destroyed after Rome sacked Corinth in 146 BC.

dare-22270.label: Heraion
dare-22270.description: Sanctuary of Hera Akraia/Limenia on the Perachora peninsula in Corinthia, with an apsidal temple dating to the 8th century BCE, one of the earliest Greek temples known; cult continued until Corinth's destruction in 146 BCE.

dare-22613.label: Heraion Argolis
dare-22613.description: The Argive Heraion, chief sanctuary of Hera between Argos and Mycenae, with an Archaic temple burned in 423 BCE and rebuilt by the architect Eupolemos; excavated extensively by the American School of Classical Studies from 1892.

dare-22650.label: Labraunda
dare-22650.description: Carian sanctuary of Zeus Labraundos in the mountains above Mylasa, greatly monumentalized in the 4th century BCE by the Hecatomnid satraps Mausolus and Idrieus as their dynastic shrine, reached by a monumental sacred way.

dare-22896.label: *Hercules Curinus
dare-22896.description: Italic and later Roman sanctuary of Hercules Curinus near Sulmona (ancient Superaequum/Corfinium area), built on a multi-terraced hillside modeled on Praeneste and Tivoli and enlarged after the Social War (89 BCE); a bronze cult statue of Hercules survives.

dare-25431.label: Tara
dare-25431.description: The Hill of Tara in County Meath, Ireland, ceremonial and assembly site associated with the legendary High Kings of Ireland, containing the Iron Age Rath of the Synods, Mound of the Hostages passage tomb, and the standing Lia Fáil stone.

dare-25704.label: Jordan Hill
dare-25704.description: Romano-Celtic temple on Jordan Hill near Weymouth, Dorset, founded c. 69-79 CE and used into the late 4th century; excavations revealed a shaft with ritual deposits of coins, pottery and bird/animal remains beneath the cella.

dare-26493.label: Olympieion
dare-26493.description: Archaic Doric Temple of Olympian Zeus (Olympieion) on the Polichne hill outside Syracuse, built in the early 6th century BCE, one of the oldest peripteral stone temples in Sicily; two columns still stand.

dare-26500.label: Sciliar
dare-26500.description: The Sciliar/Schlern plateau in South Tyrol held a Bronze Age and Iron Age high-altitude sacrificial site (Brandopferplatz), one of several Alpine peak cult places yielding numerous bronze votive objects, documented in South Tyrolean archaeological surveys (Haupt et al.).

dare-36637.label: Kafr Zabad
dare-36637.description: Kafr Zabad in the Bekaa valley preserves two Roman antae temples of the 2nd century AD on a hill above the village, now reduced mostly to foundations, with a nearby rock relief of a Roman goddess (probably Venus).

dare-36681.label: Aigaion Antron
dare-36681.description: Aigaion Antron is the Psychro (Dictaean) Cave on Mount Dicte, Crete, identified since antiquity as Zeus's birth cave where Rhea hid him from Cronus; excavations found Minoan-to-Roman votive bronzes, double axes and pottery.

dare-37063.label: Hochtor
dare-37063.description: A Celto-Roman "pass sanctuary" at the Hochtor (2504m) on the Grossglockner route, Europe's highest-altitude shrine; 1992-95 excavations found a bronze Hercules statue (first found 1933), fragments of 20+ votive statues, and ~200 Celtic and Roman coins left by travelers.

dare-37082.label: Mar Samuel, Simeon
dare-37082.description: Mor Gabriel Monastery in Tur Abdin was founded in 397 AD by the ascetics Mor Shmuel (Samuel) and Mor Shemun (Simeon) of Qartmin; it became the episcopal seat of Tur Abdin (615-1049) and remains one of the oldest continuously active Christian monasteries.

dare-37121.label: Aphrodite Aphakitis
dare-37121.description: The oracular temple of Aphrodite Aphacitis at Afqa (Aphaca), below the grotto source of the Adonis river, was notorious for ritual prostitution and was torn down on Emperor Constantine's orders in the 4th century AD, per Eusebius.

dare-37131.label: Yammune
dare-37131.description: Yammoune's Phoenician-Roman temple ruins, dedicated to Astarte/Venus, stand near the spring feeding Lake Yammoune; a rock inscription records Emperor Hadrian declaring the area a protected juniper reserve in 134 AD.

dare-37170.label: Can Modolell
dare-37170.description: Roman rural sanctuary at Cabrera de Mar (Maresme, Catalonia), flourishing 1st-2nd c. AD, apparently first dedicated to Neptune and a goddess and later a Mithraeum with an inscribed altar; continuity into the medieval period as the hermitage of Sant Joan.

dare-37357.label: Alahan
dare-37357.description: Alahan Monastery/pilgrimage complex in ancient Isauria (Mersin Province, Turkey), built in two phases: mid-5th century under Emperor Leo I and late 5th century under Emperor Zeno; two churches, a baptistery and necropolis served monks and pilgrims into the 7th century.

dare-38773.label: Ursins
dare-38773.description: Gallo-Roman fanum-type temple at Ursins (Vaud, Switzerland), built in the 1st century AD and used until the 4th, dedicated to Mercury and Mars Caturix; part of a 30-hectare regional religious center with at least three temples, baths and an amphitheater.

dare-39956.label: Cancho Roano
dare-39956.description: Cancho Roano, a Tartessian/Orientalizing-period palace-sanctuary near Zalamea de la Serena (Badajoz, Spain), occupied from the mid-8th/6th century BC; an eleven-room U-shaped mudbrick complex around a courtyard, ritually burned and buried c. 375 BC.

dare-41386.label: Grotta della Sibilla
dare-41386.description: A Roman-era rock-cut gallery on the shore of Lake Avernus (Campi Flegrei), popularly called 'Grotta della Sibilla' (or Bagno della Sibilla) after the myth of the underworld oracle; distinct from the true Cave of the Cumaean Sibyl at Cumae, its actual function was likely military/engineering, linked to Agrippa's Portus Iulius works.

dare-41885.label: Tempio di Apollo
dare-41885.description: The so-called 'Temple of Apollo' on the eastern shore of Lake Avernus is in fact the domed frigidarium of a large Roman imperial-era bath complex (probably Hadrianic, 2nd c. AD, c. 36m internal diameter), traditionally named for Apollo through the lake's association with the underworld oracle.

dare-41946.label: Postoloboso
dare-41946.description: Vettonian rural sanctuary near the confluence of the Alardos gorge and the Tiétar river, dedicated to the indigenous god Vaelicus; yielded around 20 Latin votive altars and granite verraco sculptures linked to the Vettonian oppidum of El Raso.

dare-42221.label: Butte
dare-42221.description: Gallic-to-Gallo-Roman rural sanctuary at "la Butte du Moulin à Vent", Bennecourt, occupied 2nd century BC-4th century AD; excavations (1982-88) traced its growth from a small Gallic timber shrine into a walled precinct enclosing three stone temples, yielding some 25,000 finds.

dare-42291.label: Scoglietto
dare-42291.description: Sanctuary of Diana Umbronensis on the Scoglietto promontory (Alberese, Maremma), attested by a marble dedication to the goddess of the Ombrone river; religious structures dated 1st century BC-mid 4th century AD, with votive lamps, coins, glass and two statues of Diana, abandoned after Theodosius's ban on pagan cult.

dare-42517.label: Qasr ed-Dabaschiya
dare-42517.description: Roman-period settlement (Ain el-Dabashiya) in the northern Kharga Oasis with a large mud-brick temple and a pigeon tower, dated to the 3rd-4th century AD and supplied by a complex well-based irrigation system; documented by the North Kharga Oasis Survey.

dare-42518.label: Ain et-Tarakwa
dare-42518.description: Ain el-Tarakwa, a Roman-to-Christian-period site (1st-5th century AD) in the northern Kharga Oasis with a small stone temple, a mud-brick basilica and settlement, and an extensive cemetery; recorded by the North Kharga Oasis Survey.

dare-42563.label: Tiffen
dare-42563.description: A prehistoric Celtic cult site was later succeeded by a Roman Jupiter temple (2nd-4th century AD) on the hill at Tiffen, on the spot now occupied by the parish church of St James; a Roman quarry operated nearby and reused Roman stones are built into the church's walls.

dare-43284.label: Aaiha
dare-43284.description: Roman temple at Aaiha in the Bekaa Valley, completed in 92 AD, measuring roughly 11.5 x 14.4 m with an entrance to underground vaults; only its western part survived by the mid-19th century, and it is now entirely destroyed, its blocks reused by villagers.

dare-43285.label: Deir El Aachayer
dare-43285.description: Substantial Graeco-Roman temple (c. 30 m foundations) in a formerly Ituraean part of the Bekaa Valley, dedicated to unknown "gods of Kiboreia"; a Greek inscription dated to AD 242 names the high priest Beeliabos, also called Diototos, son of Abedanos.

dare-43286.label: Dakoue
dare-43286.description: Roman temple behind the village of Dakoue retains a central courtyard and a three-column front colonnade with Corinthian mouldings; it was later converted into a church, reached via an opening in its west wall.

dare-43748.label: Mar Behnam
dare-43748.description: Syriac Orthodox shrine (martyrion) south of Mosul marking the tomb of the 4th-century martyrs Behnam and Sarah, built atop the ancient tell of Tell al-Khidr; its earliest surviving fabric dates to the 12th-13th centuries.

dare-44403.label: Pagans Hill
dare-44403.description: Octagonal Romano-Celtic temple at Chew Stoke, Somerset, built in the late 3rd century probably for Mercury as part of a pilgrimage complex with guesthouses and a holy well; excavated by Philip Rahtz, 1949-1953.

dare-44510.label: Yanta
dare-44510.description: Roman temple of the 2nd century AD at Yanta preserving its rectangular peribola, main entrance, and lintel; thought to overlie an earlier Semitic sanctuary, with a necropolis on the crag above.

dare-44511.label: Saraain El Faouqa
dare-44511.description: Roman temple in the village, part of the Beqaa Valley temple group; the cella walls have vanished but the podium survives, alongside a carved door frame, ceiling block, and column fragments found nearby.

dare-44512.label: Libbaya
dare-44512.description: Roman temple of the 2nd century AD known as Ain/Ayn Libbaya, classified by George Taylor among the Temples of Mount Hermon; included on Lebanon's UNESCO Tentative List for Sacred Mount Hermon.

dare-44514.label: Bakka
dare-44514.description: Roman prostylos temple (per George Taylor) at Bakka with standing north and south walls and a surviving podium floor; an underground crypt was reached through a house later built over the site.

dare-44902.label: Scoppieto
dare-44902.description: A rural 4th-century-BCE sanctuary at Scoppieto was overbuilt in the late 1st century BCE by a large terra sigillata pottery workshop, active into the 1st century CE, whose stamped tableware has been found as far as Carthage and Alexandria.

dare-4963.label: Zillis
dare-4963.description: A late-Roman cult cave near Zillis, in ritual use c. 260-500 CE, yielded several hundred bronze and silver coins, votive plaques, snake-motif vessels, and images of Mercury and Luna, likely a shrine to an eastern-influenced deity, possibly Mithras.

dare-7863.label: Aquae Segetae
dare-7863.description: A Flavian-era healing spa and pilgrimage sanctuary at Sceaux-du-Gâtinais centered on a sacred spring dedicated to the fertility goddess Segeta, with a temple, peristyle, and an adjoining 104-meter-diameter theater; it flourished in the 2nd century CE.

pl-900017.label: Amarna
pl-900017.description: Akhenaten founded this capital, Akhetaten, around 1346 BCE as the cult center of the sun-disc Aten; it featured the Great Temple of Aten and was largely abandoned within two decades of his death.

pleiades:676120271.label: Basilica
pleiades:676120271.description: The Klematios (Clematius) Basilica, a 5th-century ruined early Christian church on the slope of Mount Lycabettus in Athens, among the city's earliest churches; its floor mosaics are now displayed in the Byzantine and Christian Museum.

vici:vici-17724.label: Santa Caterina di Pittinurri, Basiliche di Cornu
vici:vici-17724.description: Part of the Columbaris early Christian complex near ancient Cornus (Sardinia), whose funerary basilica with baptistery (3rd-4th c.) was followed by two further basilicas in the 5th-6th centuries; Cornus became the island's episcopal seat after Constantine.

vici:vici-17760.label: Julian Basilica, Corinth
vici:vici-17760.description: The Julian Basilica, built at the east end of Corinth's Roman forum between 2 BCE and the late Augustan period, housed the largest collection of Julio-Claudian imperial statuary in Greece (Julius Caesar, Augustus, Tiberius) and stood until the 4th century CE.

vici:vici-17804.label: Basilica C, Philippi
vici:vici-17804.description: Basilica C at Philippi, a lavish 6th-century three-aisled Early Christian basilica with narthex, transept and double ambo, part of the archaeological site associated with Paul's mission to the Philippians.

vici:vici-18079.label: Bahira Basilica
vici:vici-18079.description: A 3rd-century Roman basilica at Bosra converted into a church in the 4th century, traditionally identified as the site (the 'Monastery of Bahira') where a Christian monk is said to have met the young Muhammad and foretold his prophethood.

vici:vici-18397.label: Sirmium, Imperial Basilica
vici:vici-18397.description: Basilica within the tetrarchic-era imperial palace at Sirmium, built in the late 3rd–early 4th century AD as a residence for co-emperors including Diocletian and Constantine I; the palace complex was excavated from 1957 after accidental discovery.

vici:vici-18954.label: Sabratha, Basilica
vici:vici-18954.description: Forum basilica of Sabratha, rebuilt on orders of Emperor Justinian in the 6th century AD (mentioned by his courtier Procopius) as a three-naved Christian hall with a raised presbytery and a famous mosaic floor depicting the soul's ascent to heaven.

vici:vici-19898.label: Basilica
vici:vici-19898.description: Civil basilica of Volubilis in Roman Mauretania Tingitana, completed under Emperor Macrinus in 217 AD and modeled on the basilica at Leptis Magna; a two-storey hall about 42 m long adjoining the forum and Capitolium.

vici:vici-22726.label: Baelo Claudia - basilica
vici:vici-22726.description: Forum basilica of the Roman town of Baelo Claudia near Tarifa, Spain, used for judicial and administrative business alongside the adjacent curia; the town flourished under Claudius on the strength of its fish-salting industry before declining in the 3rd century AD.

vici:vici-23664.label: Basilica Iulia
vici:vici-23664.description: Civil basilica in the Roman Forum begun by Julius Caesar in 46 BC on the site of the older Basilica Sempronia, completed and dedicated by Augustus in 12 AD to his grandsons Gaius and Lucius Caesar, housing the law courts of the centumviri.

vici:vici-24196.label: Basilica
vici:vici-24196.description: Forum basilica of the Roman colony Colonia Iulia Equestris (Nyon), founded by Julius Caesar around 45 BC for veteran cavalrymen; excavations since 1974 revealed two successive basilicas at the city's political and religious center.

vici:vici-24259.label: Aphrodisias in Caria
vici:vici-24259.description: Aphrodisias, a Carian city famed for its sanctuary of Aphrodite, marble quarries and sculpture school, and extensive Roman-era public buildings including the Sebasteion, stadium, and theatre.

vici:vici-24264.label: Civil Basilica in Aphrodisias
vici:vici-24264.description: Civil Basilica of Aphrodisias, a three-aisled public hall (about 145 x 30 m) off the South Agora, dedicated to the Flavian emperors in the late 1st century AD; its entrance wall bears Diocletian's Edict on Maximum Prices, inscribed in Latin in 301 AD.

vici:vici-24551.label: Basilika
vici:vici-24551.description: Civic basilica of the Roman vicus of Lousonna (Lausanne-Vidy) on Lake Geneva, forming the forum complex with the town's temple and sanctuary; a large hall roughly 71 by 19 m, dated by excavators to around AD 40 with later additions.

vici:vici-25724.label: Corinthus [Korinthos], North Basilica
vici:vici-25724.description: A public building north of the Roman forum at Corinth, excavated by Oscar Broneer during the 1925 campaign and published as 'Area North of Basilica' in the American Journal of Archaeology (1926).

vici:vici-25967.label: Xanthos, Roman Basilica
vici:vici-25967.description: Civic basilica lining the west side of the Cardo in Roman Xanthos, a three-aisled portico structure about 70 m long, construction begun in the late 1st century AD and completed in the 2nd century.

vici:vici-26362.label: Smyrna, Basilica
vici:vici-26362.description: Monumental basilica on the north wing of the Agora of Smyrna, a three-storey building about 160 by 29 m used by imperial officials and city magistrates for courts and public business; one of the largest basilicas of the Roman Empire after Trajan's Basilica in Rome, rebuilt after the AD 178 earthquake.

vici:vici-26669.label: Adada in Pisidia, Basilica
vici:vici-26669.description: One of two late-antique three-aisled basilicas at Adada, a Pisidian hill city otherwise noted for its well-preserved 2nd/3rd-century imperial temples, theatre, and agora.

vici:vici-27443.label: Basilica, Ostia
vici:vici-27443.description: Basilica on the west side of Ostia's forum, dated to the late 1st century AD and used for judicial hearings and commercial business; linked to the forum by a double portico whose marble reliefs depicted episodes from Rome's foundation legend.

vici:vici-27771.label: Durovigutum Basilica
vici:vici-27771.description: Single-aisled basilica (probably a town hall) built at Durovigutum (Godmanchester, Roman Britain) in the early 3rd century AD, c. 24m by 12.9m in Barnack ragstone and flint, possibly linked to Caracalla's empire-wide citizenship grant of 212/214 AD.

vici:vici-28154.label: Civitas Tropaensium
vici:vici-28154.description: Civitas Tropaensium, a Roman municipium near Adamclisi (Scythia Minor) that grew up beside Trajan's Tropaeum Traiani monument, dedicated 109 AD to commemorate his Dacian War victory; its large 4th-century forensic basilica stood near the fortress center, alongside several later Christian basilicas.

vici:vici-30109.label: Oescus, Basilica
vici:vici-30109.description: Civic basilica of Colonia Ulpia Oescus, a Roman colony on the Danube near Gigen (Bulgaria) founded under Trajan c. 106-109 AD; the three-aisled hall measured roughly 100m by 24-25m and hosted trade and judicial proceedings.

vici:vici-31374.label: Ephesus, N Stoa of Agora - "Basilica"
vici:vici-31374.description: Basilica Stoa on the north side of Ephesus's State Agora, converted from an earlier Hellenistic stoa under Augustus; a two-storey, three-aisled Ionic hall about 160m long used for courts and commerce, where statues of Augustus and Livia were later found.

vici:vici-39918.label: Baelo Claudia, Basilica
vici:vici-39918.description: Basilica of Baelo Claudia, a Roman municipium on Spain's Strait of Gibraltar coast; built c. 50-70 AD at the rear of the forum as the seat of the law courts, where a statue of Trajan was later found among the ruins.

vici:vici-42160.label: Aquileia, Basilica
vici:vici-42160.description: Civil basilica closing the south side of Aquileia's forum, erected in the 1st century AD and enlarged in the 2nd; a nave-and-aisle hall with Medusa and Jupiter Ammon reliefs, used for judicial and administrative business (distinct from the later Christian basilica church at the site).

vici:vici-42972.label: Basilika
vici:vici-42972.description: Forum basilica of Augusta Raurica near Basel; the forum's stone buildings, including the basilica, replaced earlier timber structures from c. 20-50 AD and were rebuilt after a fire gutted the complex around 150 AD.

vici:vici-42992.label: Basilika
vici:vici-42992.description: Civil basilica of Roman Egnatia (Gnathia) on Puglia's Adriatic coast, part of the forum complex astride the Via Traiana; it included the Hall of the Three Graces, named for a sculptural group now held in the site's museum.

vici:vici-43065.label: Basilica
vici:vici-43065.description: The great apsidal audience hall ("basilica") of the Villa Romana del Casale near Piazza Armerina, a lavish late Roman villa of the 4th century AD; the 100-Roman-foot throne room was floored and walled in colored marble and porphyry.

vici:vici-43080.label: Basilica
vici:vici-43080.description: Civic basilica beside the forum of Aquincum's civil town, a 3rd-century AD rectangular hall used for legal proceedings, markets, and public assembly in this provincial capital of Pannonia (modern Budapest).

vici:vici-43103.label: Basilica
vici:vici-43103.description: Basilica of the forum complex at Cambodunum (modern Kempten), first capital of the Roman province of Raetia from the 1st century AD, where court sessions were held next to the town's market square.

vici:vici-50810.label: Civitas Tropaensium, Basilica Cisterna
vici:vici-50810.description: The "Basilica Cisterna," a 3rd-century civic basilica forensis with an underlying water cistern at Civitas Tropaensium (Adamclisi), the city that grew beside Trajan's victory monument commemorating his Dacian wars of 101-106 AD.

vici:vici-51111.label: Nesactium, Northern basilica
vici:vici-51111.description: The smaller, older of twin 5th-century Early Christian basilicas at Nesactium in Istria, used for baptism and religious ceremony, with a baptistery, catechumenumium, and cemetery chapels along its side walls.

vici:vici-55560.label: Rosellae, Basilica dei Bassi
vici:vici-55560.description: The "Basilica dei Bassi," a 1st-century AD hall on the north side of the forum at Rusellae (Roselle) in Tuscany, its marble-clad interior displaying inscribed statues of the local Bassus family for whom it is named.

vici:vici-64541.label: Basilica
vici:vici-64541.description: Civil basilica on the west side of the Roman forum at Torreparedones (ancient Ituci Virtus Iulia, near Baena), built in the 1st century AD; a rectangular hall of about 350 m² used for justice and civic business.

vici:vici-64746.label: Basilice north
vici:vici-64746.description: One of two churches in the Christian quarter of Cuicul (Djémila), Numidia, built alongside the Basilica of Cresconius in the late 4th–early 5th century as part of a complex with crypts and a monumental baptistery.

vici:vici-64747.label: Basilice of Cresconius
vici:vici-64747.description: Principal church of the Christian quarter at Cuicul (Djémila), founded by Bishop Cresconius around 400-411; a nave-and-aisles basilica roughly 40 by 28 meters, paired with a second basilica, crypts, and baptistery.

vici:vici-70119.label: Smitthus, Basilica
vici:vici-70119.description: Roman forum basilica at Simitthus (Chemtou), a marble-quarrying town in Numidia; only the building's massive apse (c. 6.9 m diameter, 3.45 m deep) survives, from a forum complex dated to the 3rd–4th century AD.

vici:vici-70308.label: Large basilica
vici:vici-70308.description: Also known as the Bishop's Basilica of Philippopolis, this mid-4th-century Christian church (86 x 38.5 m) is the largest early-Christian basilica found in Bulgaria, famed for roughly 2,000 m² of bird and geometric floor mosaics.

vici:vici-79042.label: Roman basilica
vici:vici-79042.description: The civil basilica (curia) on the north side of the Roman forum at Paestum, a three-aisled rectangular hall built in the 1st century BC where the town council met and magistrates administered justice.

vici:vici-9966.label: Basilika Lopodunum (Ladenburg)
vici:vici-9966.description: Monumental basilica of the forum at Lopodunum (Ladenburg), built under Trajan as the civic center of a Neckarsueben civitas; with the forum it measured 130 x 84 m, the largest known Roman building complex in southern Germany.
